;;; swamp-present.el --- Build reveal.js decks with @webframp/presentation -*- lexical-binding: t; -*-
;;
;; Author: Sean Escriva <sean.escriva@gmail.com>
;; Version: 0.1.0
;; Package-Requires: ((emacs "29.1") (transient "0.5.0"))
;; Keywords: tools, outlines, hypermedia
;; SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
;;
;; This file is NOT part of GNU Emacs.
;;
;;; Commentary:
;;
;; Build, preview, outline and print the Org or Markdown deck in the
;; current buffer through the @webframp/presentation swamp extension.
;; Every build is stored as versioned swamp data; this file only runs swamp
;; commands and reads their output.
;;
;; Setup, once per swamp repository:
;;
;;   swamp extension pull @webframp/presentation
;;   swamp model create @webframp/presentation/deck talks
;;
;; Commands (also under `swamp-present-dispatch', and as "p" in
;; `swamp-dispatch'):
;;
;;   `swamp-present-build'    build the deck
;;   `swamp-present-preview'  build it and open it in a browser
;;   `swamp-present-outline'  list slides, notes coverage, missing images
;;   `swamp-present-pdf'      build it, print it to PDF and open the PDF
;;
;; With a prefix argument, build and preview make a self-contained deck
;; that works offline.
;;
;;; Code:

(require 'swamp)
(require 'transient)
(require 'json)
(require 'seq)

;;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
;;; Customization
;;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

(defgroup swamp-present nil
  "Build reveal.js decks with the @webframp/presentation extension."
  :group 'swamp
  :prefix "swamp-present-")

(defcustom swamp-present-deck "talks"
  "Name of the @webframp/presentation/deck model instance to build with.
An Org buffer can name another with a #+SWAMP_DECK: keyword."
  :type 'string
  :safe #'stringp
  :group 'swamp-present)

(defcustom swamp-present-output-directory nil
  "Directory for previewed HTML and PDF files.
When nil, use `temporary-file-directory'.  Files are named after the deck,
so each preview overwrites the last and a browser tab can simply reload."
  :type '(choice (const :tag "Temporary directory" nil) directory)
  :group 'swamp-present)

(defvar-local swamp-present-name nil
  "Deck name for this buffer, or nil to let swamp derive it from the file.
Set it as a file-local variable when two sources share a file name.")
(put 'swamp-present-name 'safe-local-variable
     (lambda (v) (and (stringp v) (string-match-p "\\`[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*\\'" v))))

;;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
;;; Helpers
;;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

(defconst swamp-present--log-buffer "*swamp-present*"
  "Buffer that collects swamp's error output and build warnings.")

(defun swamp-present--deck ()
  "Return the deck instance for the current buffer."
  (or (and (derived-mode-p 'org-mode)
           (save-excursion
             (save-restriction
               (widen)
               (goto-char (point-min))
               (let ((case-fold-search t))
                 (when (re-search-forward
                        "^#\\+SWAMP_DECK:[ \t]*\\([^ \t\n]+\\)" nil t)
                   (match-string-no-properties 1))))))
      swamp-present-deck))

(defun swamp-present--source ()
  "Return the current buffer's file, saving it first if it has changes."
  (let ((file (buffer-file-name)))
    (unless file
      (user-error "This buffer is not visiting a file"))
    (unless (string-match-p "\\.\\(org\\|md\\|markdown\\|mdown\\|mkd\\)\\'" file)
      (user-error "Not an Org or Markdown file: %s" file))
    (when (and (buffer-modified-p)
               (y-or-n-p (format "Save %s before building? "
                                 (file-name-nondirectory file))))
      (save-buffer))
    (expand-file-name file)))

(defun swamp-present--method-args (deck method source &rest inputs)
  "Return swamp arguments to run METHOD on DECK for SOURCE.
INPUTS are extra \"key=value\" strings passed with --input."
  (append (list "model" "method" "run" deck method
                "--input" (concat "source=" source))
          (when swamp-present-name
            (list "--input" (concat "name=" swamp-present-name)))
          (mapcan (lambda (i) (list "--input" i)) inputs)
          (list "--json")))

(defun swamp-present--record (result)
  "Return the attributes of the resource RESULT's method wrote.
Each method of the deck model writes exactly one resource; its files carry
no attributes."
  (alist-get 'attributes
             (seq-find (lambda (a) (alist-get 'attributes a))
                       (alist-get 'dataArtifacts result))))

(defun swamp-present--log (format-string &rest args)
  "Append FORMAT-STRING with ARGS to the log buffer."
  (with-current-buffer (get-buffer-create swamp-present--log-buffer)
    (goto-char (point-max))
    (insert (apply #'format format-string args) "\n")))

(defun swamp-present--parse (text)
  "Parse TEXT as swamp's JSON output, or return nil."
  (condition-case nil
      (json-parse-string text :object-type 'alist :array-type 'list)
    (error nil)))

(defun swamp-present--run (args on-success)
  "Run swamp with ARGS asynchronously, then call ON-SUCCESS with its result.
The result is swamp's parsed JSON.  A failure is reported in the echo area
and its error output is kept in the log buffer."
  (let* ((out (generate-new-buffer " *swamp-present-out*"))
         (err (generate-new-buffer " *swamp-present-err*"))
         (default-directory (or (and swamp-repo-dir
                                     (file-name-as-directory
                                      (expand-file-name swamp-repo-dir)))
                                default-directory)))
    (make-process
     :name "swamp-present"
     :buffer out
     :stderr err
     :command (append (list swamp-executable) (swamp--base-args) args)
     :noquery t
     :sentinel
     (lambda (proc _event)
       (unless (process-live-p proc)
         (unwind-protect
             (let* ((result (swamp-present--parse
                             (with-current-buffer out (buffer-string))))
                    (status (alist-get 'status result))
                    (stderr (with-current-buffer err (buffer-string))))
               (if (and (= (process-exit-status proc) 0)
                        (equal status "succeeded"))
                   (funcall on-success result)
                 (swamp-present--log "%s" stderr)
                 (message "swamp: %s"
                          (or (alist-get 'error result)
                              (format "%s failed (exit %d); see %s"
                                      (nth 4 args)
                                      (process-exit-status proc)
                                      swamp-present--log-buffer)))))
           (kill-buffer out)
           (when (buffer-live-p err) (kill-buffer err))))))))

(defun swamp-present--fetch (deck data-name)
  "Return the content of DECK's file DATA-NAME as a unibyte string.
swamp prints text files as they are and binary files as base64, each with
one trailing newline."
  (with-temp-buffer
    (set-buffer-multibyte nil)
    (let* ((coding-system-for-read 'binary)
           (predicate (format "model(%S) && name == %S" deck data-name))
           (exit (apply #'call-process swamp-executable nil '(t nil) nil
                        (append (swamp--base-args)
                                (list "data" "query" predicate
                                      "--select" "content")))))
      (unless (= exit 0)
        (user-error "swamp could not read %s from %s" data-name deck))
      (goto-char (point-max))
      (when (eq (char-before) ?\n) (delete-char -1))
      (when (= (buffer-size) 0)
        (user-error "%s has no %s yet" deck data-name))
      (buffer-string))))

(defun swamp-present--output-file (name extension)
  "Return the preview file for deck NAME with EXTENSION."
  (expand-file-name (format "swamp-present-%s.%s" name extension)
                    (or swamp-present-output-directory
                        temporary-file-directory)))

(defun swamp-present--write (file bytes)
  "Write unibyte BYTES to FILE."
  (let ((coding-system-for-write 'binary))
    (with-temp-file file
      (set-buffer-multibyte nil)
      (insert bytes)))
  file)

(defun swamp-present--report-build (deck record)
  "Echo the outcome of a build RECORD of DECK and log its warnings."
  (let ((warnings (alist-get 'warnings record)))
    (dolist (w warnings)
      (swamp-present--log "%s/%s: %s" deck (alist-get 'name record) w))
    (message "%s %s: %d slides%s%s"
             (if (eq (alist-get 'unchanged record) t) "Unchanged" "Built")
             (alist-get 'name record)
             (alist-get 'slideCount record)
             (if (eq (alist-get 'selfContained (alist-get 'reveal record)) t)
                 ", self-contained" "")
             (if warnings
                 (format ", %d warnings (see %s)" (length warnings)
                         swamp-present--log-buffer)
               ""))))

(defun swamp-present--build (self-contained then)
  "Build the current buffer's deck, then call THEN with deck and record.
SELF-CONTAINED inlines every reveal.js file."
  (let ((deck (swamp-present--deck))
        (source (swamp-present--source)))
    (message "Building %s..." (file-name-nondirectory source))
    (swamp-present--run
     (apply #'swamp-present--method-args deck "build" source
            (when self-contained (list "selfContained=true")))
     (lambda (result)
       (let ((record (swamp-present--record result)))
         (swamp-present--report-build deck record)
         (when then (funcall then deck record)))))))

;;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
;;; Commands
;;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

;;;###autoload
(defun swamp-present-build (&optional self-contained)
  "Build the deck in the current buffer.
With prefix argument SELF-CONTAINED, inline every reveal.js file so the
deck works offline."
  (interactive "P")
  (swamp-present--build self-contained nil))

;;;###autoload
(defun swamp-present-preview (&optional self-contained)
  "Build the deck in the current buffer and open it in a browser.
With prefix argument SELF-CONTAINED, build a deck that works offline."
  (interactive "P")
  (swamp-present--build
   self-contained
   (lambda (deck record)
     (let* ((name (alist-get 'name record))
            (file (swamp-present--write
                   (swamp-present--output-file name "html")
                   (swamp-present--fetch deck (format "deck-%s-html" name)))))
       (browse-url-of-file file)))))

;;;###autoload
(defun swamp-present-pdf ()
  "Build the deck in the current buffer, print it to PDF and open the PDF."
  (interactive)
  (let ((source (swamp-present--source)))
    (swamp-present--build
     nil
     (lambda (deck record)
       (let ((name (alist-get 'name record)))
         (message "Printing %s..." name)
         (swamp-present--run
          (apply #'swamp-present--method-args deck "export_pdf" source nil)
          (lambda (result)
            (let* ((pdf (swamp-present--record result))
                   (encoded (swamp-present--fetch
                             deck (format "deck-%s-pdf" name)))
                   (file (swamp-present--write
                          (swamp-present--output-file name "pdf")
                          (base64-decode-string encoded))))
              (message "%s: %d pages%s" name
                       (alist-get 'pages (alist-get 'pdf pdf))
                       (if (eq (alist-get 'unchanged pdf) t)
                           " (unchanged)" ""))
              (find-file-other-window file)))))))))

(defun swamp-present--outline-rows (record)
  "Return tabulated-list rows for the slides in outline RECORD."
  (let ((i 0))
    (mapcar (lambda (s)
              (setq i (1+ i))
              (let ((notes (alist-get 'notesWords s)))
                (list i (vector (alist-get 'index s)
                                (let ((title (alist-get 'title s)))
                                  (if (string-empty-p title) "(untitled)" title))
                                (if (eq notes 0)
                                    (propertize "none" 'face 'warning)
                                  (number-to-string notes))
                                (number-to-string
                                 (length (alist-get 'images s)))))))
            (alist-get 'slides record))))

;;;###autoload
(defun swamp-present-outline ()
  "Show the slides of the deck in the current buffer, without building it.
Lists each slide's words of speaker notes and images, and reports images
that do not exist."
  (interactive)
  (let ((deck (swamp-present--deck))
        (source (swamp-present--source)))
    (swamp-present--run
     (swamp-present--method-args deck "outline" source)
     (lambda (result)
       (let* ((record (swamp-present--record result))
              (missing (alist-get 'missingImages record)))
         (swamp--display-table
          (format "*swamp-outline:%s*" (alist-get 'name record))
          [("#" 6 nil) ("Title" 50 t) ("Notes" 7 nil) ("Images" 6 nil)]
          (swamp-present--outline-rows record))
         (message "%d slides, %d without notes%s"
                  (alist-get 'slideCount record)
                  (length (alist-get 'slidesWithoutNotes record))
                  (if missing
                      (format "; missing images: %s"
                              (string-join missing ", "))
                    "")))))))

;;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
;;; Transient menu
;;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

;;;###autoload (autoload 'swamp-present-dispatch "swamp-present" nil t)
(transient-define-prefix swamp-present-dispatch ()
  "Build reveal.js decks with @webframp/presentation."
  [["Deck"
    ("b" "build"   swamp-present-build)
    ("p" "preview" swamp-present-preview)
    ("P" "PDF"     swamp-present-pdf)]
   ["Source"
    ("o" "outline" swamp-present-outline)]])

(transient-append-suffix 'swamp-dispatch "d"
  '("p" "present" swamp-present-dispatch))

(provide 'swamp-present)
;;; swamp-present.el ends here

;;; Low-level helpers
;;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

(defun swamp--base-args ()
  "Return the base argument list (--repo-dir if configured)."
  (if swamp-repo-dir
      (list "--repo-dir" (expand-file-name swamp-repo-dir))
    nil))

(defun swamp--run-json (args)
  "Run swamp with ARGS and --json, return parsed JSON or nil on error.
ARGS is a list of strings.  The exit code determines success; JSON parse
errors are swallowed and return nil."
  (with-temp-buffer
    (let* ((full-args (append (swamp--base-args) args (list "--json")))
           (exit (apply #'call-process swamp-executable nil t nil full-args)))
      (when (= exit 0)
        (goto-char (point-min))
        (condition-case nil
            (json-parse-buffer :object-type 'alist :array-type 'list)
          (error nil))))))

(defun swamp--run-json-stream (args)
  "Run swamp with ARGS and --json, return a list of all parsed JSON objects.
Some swamp commands emit multiple newline-delimited JSON objects.
Returns a list (possibly empty) of parsed objects; never signals on parse errors."
  (with-temp-buffer
    (let ((full-args (append (swamp--base-args) args (list "--json"))))
      (apply #'call-process swamp-executable nil t nil full-args))
    (goto-char (point-min))
    (let (objects)
      (while (not (eobp))
        (condition-case nil
            (let ((obj (json-parse-buffer :object-type 'alist :array-type 'list)))
              (push obj objects))
          (error

;;; test-swamp-present.el --- ERT tests for swamp-present.el -*- lexical-binding: t; -*-
;;
;; Run with:
;;   emacs --batch -l ert -L . \
;;         -l swamp-present.el \
;;         -l test-swamp-present.el \
;;         -f ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit
;;
;; The process tests run a fake swamp executable, a shell script that
;; prints canned output, so the real argument handling and JSON parsing are
;; exercised without swamp installed.
;;
;;; Code:

(require 'ert)
(require 'cl-lib)
(require 'org)
(require 'swamp-present)

(defmacro swamp-present-test--with-fake-swamp (stdout exit &rest body)
  "Run BODY with `swamp-executable' printing STDOUT and exiting with EXIT.
The script records its arguments, one per line, in the file bound to
`args-file'."
  (declare (indent 2))
  `(let* ((dir (make-temp-file "swamp-present-test-" t))
          (args-file (expand-file-name "args" dir))
          (out-file (expand-file-name "out" dir))
          (script (expand-file-name "swamp" dir))
          (swamp-executable script)
          (swamp-repo-dir nil))
     (unwind-protect
         (progn
           (let ((coding-system-for-write 'binary))
             (write-region ,stdout nil out-file nil 'silent))
           (with-temp-file script
             (insert "#!/bin/sh\n"
                     (format "printf '%%s\\n' \"$@\" > %s\n"
                             (shell-quote-argument args-file))
                     (format "cat %s\n" (shell-quote-argument out-file))
                     (format "exit %d\n" ,exit)))
           (set-file-modes script #o755)
           ,@body)
       (delete-directory dir t))))

(defun swamp-present-test--args (file)
  "Return the arguments recorded in FILE."
  (with-temp-buffer
    (insert-file-contents file)
    (split-string (buffer-string) "\n" t)))

(defun swamp-present-test--wait ()
  "Wait for every swamp-present process to finish."
  (while (seq-some (lambda (p) (string-prefix-p "swamp-present" (process-name p)))
                   (process-list))
    (accept-process-output nil 0.05)))

;;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
;;; Loading
;;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

(ert-deftest swamp-present-commands-defined ()
  "The public commands and the transient are defined."
  (dolist (sym '(swamp-present-build swamp-present-preview
                 swamp-present-outline swamp-present-pdf
                 swamp-present-dispatch))
    (should (commandp sym))))

(ert-deftest swamp-present-in-swamp-dispatch ()
  "Loading swamp-present adds it to `swamp-dispatch' under \"p\"."
  (should (transient-get-suffix 'swamp-dispatch "p")))

;;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
;;; Arguments and records
;;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

(ert-deftest swamp-present-method-args-compose-inputs ()
  "Method arguments carry the source, the buffer's name and extra inputs."
  (with-temp-buffer
    (should (equal (swamp-present--method-args "talks" "build" "/t/a.org")
                   '("model" "method" "run" "talks" "build"
                     "--input" "source=/t/a.org" "--json")))
    (setq-local swamp-present-name "a-web")
    (should (equal (swamp-present--method-args
                    "talks" "build" "/t/a.org" "selfContained=true")
                   '("model" "method" "run" "talks" "build"
                     "--input" "source=/t/a.org"
                     "--input" "name=a-web"
                     "--input" "selfContained=true" "--json")))))

(ert-deftest swamp-present-name-local-variable-is-checked ()
  "Only data-name-safe deck names are accepted as file-local values."
  (let ((safe (get 'swamp-present-name 'safe-local-variable)))
    (should (funcall safe "talk-2"))
    (should-not (funcall safe "Talk 2"))
    (should-not (funcall safe 42))))

(ert-deftest swamp-present-deck-from-org-keyword ()
  "An Org buffer's #+SWAMP_DECK: keyword wins over the default."
  (with-temp-buffer
    (insert "#+TITLE: x\n#+swamp_deck: conference\n* One\n")
    (org-mode)
    (should (equal (swamp-present--deck) "conference")))
  (with-temp-buffer
    (insert "* One\n")
    (org-mode)
    (let ((swamp-present-deck "talks"))
      (should (equal (swamp-present--deck) "talks")))))

(ert-deftest swamp-present-record-is-the-artifact-with-attributes ()
  "The method's resource is the data artifact that carries attributes."
  (let ((result '((dataArtifacts . (((name . "deck-t-html"))
                                    ((name . "deck-t")
                                     (attributes . ((name . "t")))))))))
    (should (equal (swamp-present--record result) '((name . "t"))))))

(ert-deftest swamp-present-outline-rows ()
  "Outline rows show index, title, notes and image count."
  (let ((rows (swamp-present--outline-rows
               '((slides . (((index . "1") (title . "Intro")
                             (notesWords . 3) (images . ("a.png")))
                            ((index . "1.2") (title . "")
                             (notesWords . 0) (images . ()))))))))
    (should (equal (mapcar (lambda (r) (substring-no-properties
                                        (aref (cadr r) 2)))
                           rows)
                   '("3" "none")))
    (should (equal (aref (cadr (car rows)) 3) "1"))
    (should (equal (aref (cadr (cadr rows)) 1) "(untitled)"))))

;;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
;;; Running swamp
;;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

(ert-deftest swamp-present-run-passes-result-on-success ()
  "A succeeded run hands the parsed JSON to the callback."
  (swamp-present-test--with-fake-swamp
      "{\"status\":\"succeeded\",\"dataArtifacts\":[]}" 0
    (let ((swamp-repo-dir "/repo") got)
      (swamp-present--run '("model" "method" "run" "d" "build" "--json")
                          (lambda (r) (setq got r)))
      (swamp-present-test--wait)
      (should (equal (alist-get 'status got) "succeeded"))
      (should (equal (swamp-present-test--args args-file)
                     '("model" "method" "run" "d" "build" "--json"
                       "--repo-dir" "/repo"))))))

(ert-deftest swamp-present-run-reports-failure ()
  "A failed run shows swamp's error and never calls the callback."
  (swamp-present-test--with-fake-swamp
      "{\"error\":\"Source not found: x.org\"}" 1
    (let (called)
      (swamp-present--run '("model" "method" "run" "d" "build" "--json")
                          (lambda (_) (setq called t)))
      (swamp-present-test--wait)
      (should-not called)
      (should (string-match-p "Source not found" (current-message))))))

(ert-deftest swamp-present-fetch-strips-the-trailing-newline ()
  "Fetched content is exactly the stored bytes."
  (swamp-present-test--with-fake-swamp "<html>deck</html>\n" 0
    (should (equal (swamp-present--fetch "talks" "deck-t-html")
                   "<html>deck</html>"))
    (should (equal (swamp-present-test--args args-file)
                   '("data" "query" "model(\"talks\") && name == \"deck-t-html\""
                     "--select" "content")))))

(ert-deftest swamp-present-fetch-rejects-empty-content ()
  "An empty result is an error, not an empty file."
  (swamp-present-test--with-fake-swamp "\n" 0
    (should-error (swamp-present--fetch "talks" "deck-t-pdf")
                  :type 'user-error)))

(ert-deftest swamp-present-build-refuses-non-deck-buffers ()
  "Building needs an Org or Markdown file."
  (with-temp-buffer
    (should-error (swamp-present-build) :type 'user-error))
  (let ((file (make-temp-file "swamp-present-" nil ".txt")))
    (unwind-protect
        (with-current-buffer (find-file-noselect file)
          (unwind-protect
              (should-error (swamp-present-build) :type 'user-error)
            (kill-buffer)))
      (delete-file file))))

(ert-deftest swamp-present-write-keeps-bytes ()
  "Binary content round-trips through the preview file unchanged."
  (let ((file (make-temp-file "swamp-present-" nil ".pdf"))
        (bytes (unibyte-string 37 80 68 70 0 255 10 13)))
    (unwind-protect
        (progn
          (swamp-present--write file bytes)
          (should (equal (with-temp-buffer
                           (set-buffer-multibyte nil)
                           (let ((coding-system-for-read 'binary))
                             (insert-file-contents file))
                           (buffer-string))
                         bytes)))
      (delete-file file))))

(provide 'test-swamp-present)
;;; test-swamp-present.el ends here

;;; test-swamp-present.el --- ERT tests for swamp-present.el -*- lexical-binding: t; -*-
;;
;; Run with:
;;   emacs --batch -l ert -L . \
;;         -l swamp-present.el \
;;         -l test-swamp-present.el \
;;         -f ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit
;;
;; The process tests run a fake swamp executable, a shell script that
;; prints canned output, so the real argument handling and JSON parsing are
;; exercised without swamp installed.
;;
;;; Code:

(require 'ert)
(require 'cl-lib)
(require 'org)
(require 'swamp-present)

(defmacro swamp-present-test--with-fake-swamp (stdout exit &rest body)
  "Run BODY with `swamp-executable' printing STDOUT and exiting with EXIT.
The script records its arguments, one per line, in the file bound to
`args-file'."
  (declare (indent 2))
  `(let* ((dir (make-temp-file "swamp-present-test-" t))
          (args-file (expand-file-name "args" dir))
          (out-file (expand-file-name "out" dir))
          (script (expand-file-name "swamp" dir))
          (swamp-executable script)
          (swamp-repo-dir nil))
     (unwind-protect
         (progn
           (let ((coding-system-for-write 'binary))
             (write-region ,stdout nil out-file nil 'silent))
           (with-temp-file script
             (insert "#!/bin/sh\n"
                     (format "printf '%%s\\n' \"$@\" > %s\n"
                             (shell-quote-argument args-file))
                     (format "cat %s\n" (shell-quote-argument out-file))
                     (format "exit %d\n" ,exit)))
           (set-file-modes script #o755)
           ,@body)
       (delete-directory dir t))))

(defun swamp-present-test--args (file)
  "Return the arguments recorded in FILE."
  (with-temp-buffer
    (insert-file-contents file)
    (split-string (buffer-string) "\n" t)))

(defun swamp-present-test--wait ()
  "Wait for every swamp-present process to finish."
  (while (seq-some (lambda (p) (string-prefix-p "swamp-present" (process-name p)))
                   (process-list))
    (accept-process-output nil 0.05)))

;;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
;;; Loading
;;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

(ert-deftest swamp-present-commands-defined ()
  "The public commands and the transient are defined."
  (dolist (sym '(swamp-present-build swamp-present-preview
                 swamp-present-outline swamp-present-pdf
                 swamp-present-dispatch))
    (should (commandp sym))))

(ert-deftest swamp-present-in-swamp-dispatch ()
  "Loading swamp-present adds it to `swamp-dispatch' under \"p\"."
  (should (transient-get-suffix 'swamp-dispatch "p")))

;;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
;;; Arguments and records
;;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

(ert-deftest swamp-present-method-args-compose-inputs ()
  "Method arguments carry the source, the buffer's name and extra inputs."
  (with-temp-buffer
    (should (equal (swamp-present--method-args "talks" "build" "/t/a.org")
                   '("model" "method" "run" "talks" "build"
                     "--input" "source=/t/a.org" "--json")))
    (setq-local swamp-present-name "a-web")
    (should (equal (swamp-present--method-args
                    "talks" "build" "/t/a.org" "selfContained=true")
                   '("model" "method" "run" "talks" "build"
                     "--input" "source=/t/a.org"
                     "--input" "name=a-web"
                     "--input" "selfContained=true" "--json")))))

(ert-deftest swamp-present-name-local-variable-is-checked ()
  "Only data-name-safe deck names are accepted as file-local values."
  (let ((safe (get 'swamp-present-name 'safe-local-variable)))
    (should (funcall safe "talk-2"))
    (should-not (funcall safe "Talk 2"))
    (should-not (funcall safe 42))))

(ert-deftest swamp-present-deck-from-org-keyword ()
  "An Org buffer's #+SWAMP_DECK: keyword wins over the default."
  (with-temp-buffer
    (insert "#+TITLE: x\n#+swamp_deck: conference\n* One\n")
    (org-mode)
    (should (equal (swamp-present--deck) "conference")))
  (with-temp-buffer
    (insert "* One\n")
    (org-mode)
    (let ((swamp-present-deck "talks"))
      (should (equal (swamp-present--deck) "talks")))))

(ert-deftest swamp-present-record-is-the-artifact-with-attributes ()
  "The method's resource is the data artifact that carries attributes."
  (let ((result '((dataArtifacts . (((name . "deck-t-html"))
                                    ((name . "deck-t")
                                     (attributes . ((name . "t")))))))))
    (should (equal (swamp-present--record result) '((name . "t"))))))

(ert-deftest swamp-present-outline-rows ()
  "Outline rows show index, title, notes and image count."
  (let ((rows (swamp-present--outline-rows
               '((slides . (((index . "1") (title . "Intro")
                             (notesWords . 3) (images . ("a.png")))
                            ((index . "1.2") (title . "")
                             (notesWords . 0) (images . ()))))))))
    (should (equal (mapcar (lambda (r) (substring-no-properties
                                        (aref (cadr r) 2)))
                           rows)
                   '("3" "none")))
    (should (equal (aref (cadr (car rows)) 3) "1"))
    (should (equal (aref (cadr (cadr rows)) 1) "(untitled)"))))

;;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
;;; Running swamp
;;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

(ert-deftest swamp-present-run-passes-result-on-success ()
  "A succeeded run hands the parsed JSON to the callback."
  (swamp-present-test--with-fake-swamp
      "{\"status\":\"succeeded\",\"dataArtifacts\":[]}" 0
    (let ((swamp-repo-dir "/repo") got)
      (swamp-present--run '("model" "method" "run" "d" "build" "--json")
                          (lambda (r) (setq got r)))
      (swamp-present-test--wait)
      (should (equal (alist-get 'status got) "succeeded"))
      (should (equal (swamp-present-test--args args-file)
                     '("model" "method" "run" "d" "build" "--json"
                       "--repo-dir" "/repo"))))))

(ert-deftest swamp-present-run-reports-failure ()
  "A failed run shows swamp's error and never calls the callback."
  (swamp-present-test--with-fake-swamp
      "{\"error\":\"Source not found: x.org\"}" 1
    (let (called)
      (swamp-present--run '("model" "method" "run" "d" "build" "--json")
                          (lambda (_) (setq called t)))
      (swamp-present-test--wait)
      (should-not called)
      (should (string-match-p "Source not found" (current-message))))))

(ert-deftest swamp-present-fetch-strips-the-trailing-newline ()
  "Fetched content is exactly the stored bytes."
  (swamp-present-test--with-fake-swamp "<html>deck</html>\n" 0
    (should (equal (swamp-present--fetch "talks" "deck-t-html")
                   "<html>deck</html>"))
    (should (equal (swamp-present-test--args args-file)
                   '("data" "query" "model(\"talks\") && name == \"deck-t-html\""
                     "--select" "content")))))

(ert-deftest swamp-present-fetch-rejects-empty-content ()
  "An empty result is an error, not an empty file."
  (swamp-present-test--with-fake-swamp "\n" 0
    (should-error (swamp-present--fetch "talks" "deck-t-pdf")
                  :type 'user-error)))

(ert-deftest swamp-present-build-refuses-non-deck-buffers ()
  "Building needs an Org or Markdown file."
  (with-temp-buffer
    (should-error (swamp-present-build) :type 'user-error))
  (let ((file (make-temp-file "swamp-present-" nil ".txt")))
    (unwind-protect
        (with-current-buffer (find-file-noselect file)
          (unwind-protect
              (should-error (swamp-present-build) :type 'user-error)
            (kill-buffer)))
      (delete-file file))))

(ert-deftest swamp-present-write-keeps-bytes ()
  "Binary content round-trips through the preview file unchanged."
  (let ((file (make-temp-file "swamp-present-" nil ".pdf"))
        (bytes (unibyte-string 37 80 68 70 0 255 10 13)))
    (unwind-protect
        (progn
          (swamp-present--write file bytes)
          (should (equal (with-temp-buffer
                           (set-buffer-multibyte nil)
                           (let ((coding-system-for-read 'binary))
                             (insert-file-contents file))
                           (buffer-string))
                         bytes)))
      (delete-file file))))

# swamp.el

An Emacs transient interface for the [swamp](https://github.com/systeminit/swamp) AI-native automation CLI.

## Features

- Transient menus for all swamp commands (models, workflows, extensions, data)
- All output rendered via Emacs-native `tabulated-list-mode` and `special-mode` buffers — no terminal emulator required
- `RET` on any list row drills into a detail buffer
- Status values (`succeeded`, `failed`, `running`) are highlighted with distinct faces
- `swamp-jump-to-last-result` jumps back to the most recent result buffer
- `swamp-repo-dir` customizable for per-project repo targeting

## Requirements

- Emacs 29.1+
- [transient](https://github.com/magit/magit/tree/main/lisp) 0.5.0+
- The `swamp` CLI on your `PATH`

## Installation

### straight.el / Doom Emacs

```elisp
(package! swamp
  :recipe (:host github
           :repo "webframp/emacs-swamp"
           :files ("swamp.el")))
```

### use-package + straight.el

```elisp
(use-package swamp
  :straight (:host github :repo "webframp/emacs-swamp" :files ("swamp.el")))
```

## Usage

Call `M-x swamp-dispatch` (or bind it) to open the root transient menu:

```
Swamp AI-native automation

Models                   Workflows
m  Model                 w  Workflow
d  data query            e  Extension
                         S  summarize
                         b  last result
```

### Keybinding example

```elisp
(global-set-key (kbd "C-c s") #'swamp-dispatch)
```

### Doom Emacs keybinding

```elisp
(map! :leader :prefix "o s" "" #'swamp-dispatch)
```

### Submenus

| Menu | Key | Commands |
|---|---|---|
| Model | `m` | search (`s`), get (`g`), output get (`o`), method run (`r`), validate (`v`) |
| Workflow | `w` | search (`s`), get (`g`), run (`r`), history (`h`) |
| Extension | `e` | search (`s`), pull (`p`) |

### Direct commands

All commands are also callable directly:

| Command | Description |
|---|---|
| `swamp-model-search` | Search models; results in a table, `RET` opens detail |
| `swamp-model-get` | Show model detail (type, version, methods) |
| `swamp-model-method-run` | Run a method; blocks until complete |
| `swamp-model-output-get` | Show latest output artifact metadata |
| `swamp-model-validate` | Validate model definition with pass/fail per check |
| `swamp-workflow-search` | Search workflows; `RET` opens detail |
| `swamp-workflow-run` | Run a workflow; shows job/step tree on completion |
| `swamp-workflow-history` | List recent runs with status and duration |
| `swamp-workflow-get` | Show workflow definition detail |
| `swamp-extension-search` | Search the extension registry |
| `swamp-extension-pull` | Pull an extension; reports `name@version` on success |
| `swamp-data-query` | Run a CEL predicate against data artifacts |
| `swamp-summarize` | Show recent activity summary |
| `swamp-jump-to-last-result` | Jump to the most recently opened result buffer |

## Customization

```elisp
;; Path to the swamp executable (default: "swamp")
(setq swamp-executable "/usr/local/bin/swamp")

;; Pin commands to a specific repo directory
(setq swamp-repo-dir "~/src/my-swamp-repo")
```

## Buffer conventions

| Buffer | Mode | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `*swamp-models*` | `tabulated-list-mode` | `RET` → model detail |
| `*swamp-model:<name>*` | `special-mode` | — |
| `*swamp-run:<model>/<method>*` | `special-mode` | — |
| `*swamp-output:<name>*` | `special-mode` | — |
| `*swamp-validate:<name>*` | `special-mode` | Pass/fail per validation |
| `*swamp-workflows*` | `tabulated-list-mode` | `RET` → workflow detail |
| `*swamp-workflow:<name>*` | `special-mode` | — |
| `*swamp-workflow-run:<name>*` | `special-mode` | Job/step tree with status |
| `*swamp-history:<name>*` | `tabulated-list-mode` | — |
| `*swamp-extensions*` | `tabulated-list-mode` | — |
| `*swamp-data*` | `tabulated-list-mode` | — |
| `*swamp-summary*` | `tabulated-list-mode` | — |

## Running tests

```sh
emacs --batch -l ert \
      -l swamp.el \
      -l test-swamp.el \
      -f ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit
```

## License

GPL-3.0-or-later

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /home/sme/.claude/skills/pre-push-review

# Pre-Push Review Loop

Run a local adversarial review on uncommitted or unpushed changes. Iterate
until the review passes, then stop and ask the human for push confirmation.

## When to Use

After making changes and before pushing to a remote branch. Especially
critical for:
- Fixes to prior adversarial review findings (regression risk is high)
- Concurrent-access code (locks, sequences, distributed state)
- Any change touching error handling or fallback paths
- New code (>200 LOC) — fresh code has too much surface area for a single pass

## The Loop

```

│                                                     │
│  ┌──────────┐    ┌───────────┐    ┌──────────────┐ │
│  │  SHOW    │───►│   RUN     │───►│  EVALUATE    │ │
│  │  DIFF    │    │  GATES    │    │  VERDICT     │ │
│  └──────────┘    └───────────┘    └──────┬───────┘ │
│                        ▲                 │         │
│                        │           ┌─────┴─────┐   │
│                        │           │           │   │
│                        │         PASS        FAIL  │
│                        │           │           │   │
│                        │           ▼           ▼   │
│                        │     ┌──────────┐ ┌──────┐ │
│                        │     │  ASK TO  │ │ FIX  │ │
│                        │     │  PUSH    │ │      │ │
│                        │     └──────────┘ └──┬───┘ │
│                        │                     │     │
│                        └─────────────────────┘     │
│                                                     │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Phase 1: Show Diff

Collect the changes to review:

```bash
# Uncommitted changes against HEAD:
git diff HEAD

# Or unpushed commits against remote:
git diff origin/main...HEAD
```

Use whichever is appropriate. If there are uncommitted changes, review those.
If all changes are committed but unpushed, review the full branch diff.

## Phase 2: Run Quality Gates

Before sending to the reviewer, verify the code compiles and passes local
checks. This phase has two parts: standard gates and repo-specific gates.

### 2a. Standard Gates

Discover gates from the project's config files:

| Config file | Commands |
|-------------|----------|
| `deno.json` | `deno task check && deno task lint && deno task fmt:check && deno task test` |
| `package.json` | `npm run lint && npm run build && npm test` |
| `Cargo.toml` | `cargo check && cargo clippy && cargo test` |

If gates fail, fix them first. Do not send broken code to the reviewer.

### 2b. Repo-Specific CI Gates

Standard gates catch compile/lint/test failures. They do NOT catch structural
or convention failures that CI validates separately.

**Always check for repo-level guidance first.** Read steering files, skills,
CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, or contributing docs in the target repository. These
define what CI expects beyond standard compilation. Follow that guidance
exhaustively — run EVERY command listed, not a subset. Skipping a single
command from the checklist is the same as skipping Phase 2 entirely.

If no explicit guidance exists, fall back to these heuristics:

1. **Check CI workflow files** (`.github/workflows/`, `.gitlab-ci.yml`).
   Identify validation steps beyond standard gates and run them locally.

2. **Compare directory structure against a peer.** In repos with many
   packages of the same kind, your new addition must match the structure
   of existing ones (marker files, metadata files, test file conventions).

3. **Run repo-specific validation commands locally.** If CI runs a
   validation command, run it yourself first.

**The principle:** if CI will run it, you run it first. "It compiled and
the tests passed" is necessary but not sufficient.

### 2c. Swamp Extension Version and Manifest Gates

When changes touch swamp extensions (any directory with a `manifest.yaml`),
run these additional checks BEFORE the adversarial review. These fail
frequently and are easy to miss:

1. **Version alignment.** The `version` field in `manifest.yaml` MUST match
   the `version` field in the model's TypeScript source (`export const model =
   { version: "..." }`). If you bumped the model version, bump the manifest.
   Verify with `swamp extension version --manifest manifest.yaml --json`.

2. **Upgrade chain integrity.** If the model has an `upgrades` array, the last
   entry's `toVersion` MUST equal the model's `version` field. Every upgrade
   entry MUST have a unique `toVersion` in ascending order. A version bump
   without a corresponding upgrade entry means cached data from the previous
   version will not be migrated.

3. **Manifest format validation.** Run `swamp extension fmt manifest.yaml
   --check --json`. This catches YAML formatting issues that the push rejects.

4. **Quality gate.** Run `swamp extension quality manifest.yaml --json`.
   Verify `status: "passed"` and no degraded checks.

5. **Dry-run push.** Run `swamp extension push manifest.yaml --dry-run`.
   This exercises the full bundler, archive builder, and schema validation
   pipeline. If it fails here, it fails in CI.

**Common failure modes:**
- Bumping `model.version` but not `manifest.yaml` version
- Adding an upgrade handler but using the wrong `toVersion` string
- Forgetting to add `days` or `fetchedAt` to a new resource spec that
  requires it (schema validation fails on push)
- Leaving the old spec name in a `writeResource` call after renaming specs

## Phase 3: Adversarial Review via Subagent

The subagent MUST have the same capability as a CI adversarial reviewer.
A diff blob with prose context is insufficient — the reviewer must read
the actual source files to trace execution paths, verify cross-function
consistency, and find protocol-level issues.

### Subagent Setup

Use a general-purpose subagent (fresh context, read access to the repo). Provide:

1. **File paths to read** — tell the subagent which source files to read
   in full. The diff identifies *what* changed; the source files reveal
   *what interacts with* what changed. The subagent must read the complete
   implementation files, not just the diff.

2. **The diff** — for awareness of what's new vs existing code.

3. **Protocol and boundary context** — describe the external system's
   interface contract. For APIs: how input is parsed (line-delimited?
   shell-tokenized? JSON?). For CLI wrappers: how arguments are
   concatenated. For network protocols: framing, escaping, delimiters.
   The reviewer cannot find injection bugs without understanding the
   protocol boundary.

4. **Sibling consistency requirement** — if the code has multiple
   functions that do similar things (e.g., multiple command builders,
   multiple SSH invocations), explicitly instruct the reviewer to verify
   that ALL siblings apply the same validation/escaping/timeout patterns.
   Inconsistency between siblings is the #1 class of bug that single-pass
   reviews miss.

### Review Prompt Requirements

The subagent's review instructions MUST include these specific probes
(not just "assume broken"):

1. **Trace every interpolation site.** For each user-supplied value that
   ends up in a command string, network request, or file path: what
   characters can break the framing? Spaces, newlines, quotes, semicolons,
   pipes, backticks, dollar signs, null bytes — each has meaning in
   different contexts.

2. **Verify sibling consistency.** If function A validates input X, do
   ALL functions that accept the same class of input apply the same
   validation? List every sibling and confirm.

3. **Check timeout/resource bounds on every external call.** Every
   subprocess spawn, every network request, every fan-out: is there a
   hard deadline? What happens if it hangs? What happens if output is
   unbounded?

4. **Test with concrete breaking inputs.** For each finding, provide the
   exact input string that breaks it. "This could be a problem" is not a
   finding — "input X produces output Y which the server interprets as Z"
   is a finding.

5. **Verify the bootstrap/lifecycle path.** Can the code be invoked in
   the order the documentation describes? Are there circular dependencies
   between configuration and the methods that produce that configuration?

6. **Check truthiness vs nullability.** In JavaScript/TypeScript,
   `if (x)` skips `0`, `""`, `NaN`, `null`, `undefined`. For numeric
   parameters, `0` is often a valid value. For optional strings, `""`
   may be meaningful.

7. **Check for deferred work.** Does the change exclude, skip, stub, or
   TODO something the author identified as broken? Does the PR description
   or a code comment contain "follow-up", "until X handles it", "known
   limitation", or "out of scope" for a defect in the code being touched or
   sharing its root cause? A fix that avoids the defect (exclusion list,
   feature flag off, narrowed scope) instead of fixing it is a HIGH finding
   unless the user explicitly approved the deferral. Verify each claim the
   description makes about why the work was not done against the actual
   spec/code; a deferral rationale that is factually wrong is CRITICAL.

### Verdict Format

Require the subagent to produce:

```
### [CRITICAL|HIGH|MEDIUM|LOW] <title>
**File:** <path>
**Line(s):** <range>
**Issue:** What is wrong
**Breaking input:** The exact value that triggers the bug
**Impact:** What breaks
**Fix:** How to fix it

## VERDICT: PASS or FAIL
```

FAIL if any CRITICAL or HIGH findings exist. PASS otherwise.

## Phase 4: Evaluate Verdict

| Verdict | Action |
|---------|--------|
| PASS (no HIGH+) | Proceed to Phase 5 |
| FAIL (any HIGH+) | Fix findings, return to Phase 2 |

### On FAIL

- Fix ALL findings (HIGH, MEDIUM, and LOW). Do not defer.
- After fixing, re-run quality gates (Phase 2)
- Re-run the adversarial subagent (Phase 3) on the CURRENT source files
- The re-review MUST re-read the source files — do NOT just re-review
  the new diff. Fixes often introduce new inconsistencies.
- Do NOT push between iterations

### Minimum Iterations

- For new code (>200 LOC of implementation): run at minimum 2 review
  iterations even if the first passes. Fresh code has too much surface
  area for a single pass to catch everything.
- For fixes to existing code (<50 LOC): one passing iteration is
  sufficient.

### Iteration Cap

Maximum 5 review iterations. If still failing after 5:
- Summarize what was fixed
- List remaining findings
- Ask the human for guidance — do not push in a failing state

## Phase 5: Ask to Push

When the review passes:

1. Show a brief summary of what changed
2. State: "Local adversarial review passed. Ready to push?"
3. **Wait for explicit human confirmation**
4. Only push after the human says yes

## Rules

- NEVER push without human confirmation, even on PASS
- NEVER skip Phase 2 (quality gates) — broken code wastes review cycles
- NEVER send only a diff to the reviewer — the subagent must read the
  full source files. A diff is supplementary context, not the primary input.
- NEVER defer a finding. Fix ALL findings before the next iteration.
  Deferral is not your decision — only the human can choose to ship with
  a known issue. If you think something should be deferred, ask
  explicitly. Otherwise, fix it.
- If the same finding appears twice across iterations, try a fundamentally
  different approach rather than tweaking the same fix
- After fixing findings, the re-review must check that the fix didn't
  introduce inconsistency with sibling code. Fixing function A without
  applying the same fix to sibling functions B and C is the most common
  regression pattern.
- The subagent review has confirmation bias limitations (it reads with
  fresher eyes than you, but still runs on the same model). Expect CI to
  occasionally catch things the local loop misses — but "occasionally"
  means one finding, not six rounds of fixes. If CI finds more than one
  HIGH after your pre-push loop, the loop was run incorrectly.

# Extension Adversarial Review

After writing or **significantly modifying** extension code (anything beyond a
typo, comment tweak, or trivial rename), review against each applicable
dimension below **before running smoke tests or unit tests**. Present findings
to the user before proceeding.

This is step 4 of the Development Workflow in
[../reference.md](../reference.md#shared-development-workflow) and gates steps 5
(smoke test) and 6 (unit tests).

## When to Run

- After writing new extension code, **before** smoke tests or unit tests
  (workflow step 4 — see the
  [Adversarial Review Gate](../reference.md#adversarial-review-gate))
- After revising code in response to smoke test failures (review only changed
  dimensions)
- Before publishing with `swamp extension push`

## Recording the Review (checked at push)

`swamp extension push` checks for this review. A missing, stale, or incomplete
report surfaces as a warning the user must confirm before the push proceeds (it
is not a hard block — a benign version bump should not brick a push). The report
is bound to a content hash: any source change (or version bump) moves the report
path, so a prior review no longer matches and a fresh one is requested.

Workflow:

1. Review the code against every applicable dimension below.
2. Run `swamp extension push manifest.yaml --dry-run`. When no report exists,
   the push prints the exact report path (a content-hash-bound JSON file under
   the system temp directory). With `--json`, that finding in `warnings.review`
   also carries `skeleton`, a fill-in report object listing every applicable
   dimension with `"verdict": "pending"`. Set `SWAMP_EXTENSION_REVIEW_DIR` to
   override the base directory (useful for CI — store reports in the repo so
   they survive across runners).
3. Write the skeleton to the printed path, setting each dimension's `verdict`:
   - `pass` — the dimension is satisfied.
   - `issue` — a problem was found; add a `note`. (Surfaces as a push warning
     under the distinct ruleId `adversarial-review-dimension-issue` — separate
     from the `adversarial-review-report` ruleId used when a review is
     missing/stale/incomplete — so a CI gate keying on
     `warnings.review[].ruleId == "adversarial-review-report"` passes a
     completed review regardless of verdict while still surfacing the note. Does
     not block.)
   - `na` — the dimension does not apply (e.g. `api-contracts` for an extension
     making no HTTP calls).
   - Leave none as `pending` — a `pending` or missing verdict surfaces as a push
     warning to confirm.
   - Set `reviewedAt` to the current ISO-8601 timestamp.
4. Present the findings to the user, then run `swamp extension push`.

Report schema (the skeleton already has the right shape):

```json
{
  "extension": "@collective/name",
  "version": "2026.05.31.1",
  "reviewedAt": "2026-05-31T21:00:00Z",
  "dimensions": [
    { "id": "credentials-secrets", "verdict": "pass" },
    {
      "id": "error-handling",
      "verdict": "issue",
      "note": "delete swallows 404"
    }
  ]
}
```

The applicable dimension `id`s are the universal set plus the type-specific set
for the content kinds present (the skeleton lists exactly these). The push gate
checks that the report matches the extension name/version, covers every
applicable dimension, and has no `pending` verdicts.

## Mandatory Mechanical Verification

Execute these checks **before** the dimensional review. They catch structural
mismatches between schemas and writes that judgment-based review consistently
misses. Each check is binary — fix any failure before proceeding.

### 1. Schema-Write Conformance

For every `writeResource` call in every method:

1. Identify which spec the call targets (the spec name argument).
2. Read that spec's Zod schema — list every field.
3. Read the data object passed to `writeResource` — list every field.
4. Verify:
   - Every schema field appears in the data object.
   - No data field is absent from the schema.
   - No field is hardcoded to a placeholder (`[]`, `""`, `0`, `false`, `null`,
     `"TODO"`) when the schema implies real data.
   - The spec name matches the intent — a method writing seat data should target
     the seats spec, not a differently-shaped spec.

### 2. Truncation Honesty

For every method that paginates or caps results:

1. Find the pagination loop or result cap.
2. Verify the output spec schema includes a `truncated` (or equivalent) boolean
   field.
3. Verify the `writeResource` call sets that field — `true` when results were
   capped, `false` otherwise.

### 3. Instance Name Consistency

For every spec that multiple methods can write to:

1. List all methods that call `writeResource` for that spec.
2. Verify each method writes data conforming to the same schema shape.
3. Verify instance names don't collide across methods writing incompatible data.

This reinforces the "Instance names" dimension under Behaviors — the mechanical
check here is to explicitly enumerate and compare, not rely on a judgment call.

### 4. Schema Field Coverage

For every spec in the extension:

1. Count the schema fields.
2. Count the fields actually written across all methods that target that spec.
3. Confirm 1:1 coverage — no schema field is never written, no written field is
   absent from the schema.
4. For optional or conditional fields, verify the code path that populates them
   exists (not just that the field is declared).

### Reporting Mechanical Failures

Any mechanical check failure is a blocker — fix the code before starting the
dimensional review. In the findings report, prefix mechanical failures with
`MECHANICAL:` so they are visually distinct:

```markdown
- Schema-Write Conformance: MECHANICAL: `sync` writes `byUser: []` but
  ByUserSchema expects `{ login, role, lastActive }` — placeholder never
  populated.
```

## Output Format

Produce a structured findings report with one line per applicable dimension.
Each line is either `PASS` or `ISSUE FOUND` with detail. Use the dimensions that
apply to your extension type (universal + the relevant type-specific section).
Skip dimensions that do not apply (e.g. omit "API Contracts" for an extension
that makes no external HTTP calls — note the omission explicitly).

input.prompt:
You are an ADVERSARIAL code reviewer. Assume the code is broken and prove where. Do NOT modify any files — read and run read-only commands only (you may create scratch files under /tmp/claude-1000/review-ext/ to run experiments).

## What to review
New swamp extension `@webframp/presentation` on branch `feat/presentation` in /home/sme/src/webframp/swamp-extensions. Diff: `git -C /home/sme/src/webframp/swamp-extensions diff origin/main...HEAD`. Repo rules are in /home/sme/src/webframp/swamp-extensions/CLAUDE.md — read it; violations are findings.

READ THESE FILES IN FULL (the diff is only supplementary):
- presentation/extensions/models/presentation/deck.ts (model: build, outline, export_pdf)
- presentation/extensions/models/presentation/_lib/{pins,cache,source,engines,html,pdf}.ts
- presentation/extensions/reports/deck_summary_report.ts
- presentation/extensions/workflows/presentation-build.yaml
- presentation/manifest.yaml, README.md, RELEASE_NOTES.md, deno.json
- all *_test.ts files beside them

## What it does
Builds reveal.js decks from Org (via batch Emacs + org-re-reveal) or Markdown (pandoc, or reveal.js's browser-side markdown plugin), post-processes the HTML (inline local images as data URIs; either add SRI integrity attrs to pinned jsDelivr reveal.js 6.0.1 URLs, or inline those files fetched through a SHA-256-verified cache), stores HTML as a swamp file artifact `deck-<name>-html` and a record resource `deck-<name>`; outline writes `outline-<name>`; export_pdf prints the stored HTML with headless Chromium over the DevTools protocol and writes `deck-<name>-pdf` + `pdf-<name>`.

## Protocol boundaries (trace every value crossing them)
- Emacs: `Deno.Command(emacs, {args: ["--batch","-Q","-l",buildEl,lispDir,source,REVEAL_CDN,theme]})`, no shell. build.el (BUILD_EL string in engines.ts) consumes `command-line-args-left`. Emacs's own command-line parser processes argv: consider what a source path or theme beginning with `-` or `--eval` would do, and whether build.el clears args before Emacs acts on them. HTML is read from stdout between marker lines.
- pandoc: three invocations (`--version`, `-D revealjs`, render) with argv arrays; a generated template file and a YAML metadata file (`theme: <JSON string>`) written into a temp dir.
- Chromium: spawned with `--remote-debugging-port=0`; endpoint parsed from stderr; page URL `file://<tmp>/deck.html?print-pdf`; CDP JSON over WebSocket.
- HTML post-processing is regex-based over engine output which embeds user content (slide text, code blocks, image paths, attribute values). Look for content that breaks the segmenting of <script>/<style>/<textarea> bodies, attribute regexes, data-URI inlining of paths (path traversal: `../../etc/passwd.png`, absolute paths, file:// URIs, symlinks), and `</script>` / `</textarea>` escaping.
- Data names: `deck-${name}`, `deck-${name}-html`, etc. Names validated by DECK_NAME_PATTERN. Check collisions across specs and across decks (e.g., deck named `x-html` vs deck `x`'s HTML file; deck `x-pdf`).
- Cache: fetchVerified writes atomically; concurrency between two builds; cache dir from global arg or XDG/HOME.

## Mandatory probes
1. Trace every interpolation site with concrete breaking inputs (spaces, newlines, quotes, `$`, backticks, `-` prefixes, `..`, null bytes, unicode).
2. Sibling consistency: build/outline/export_pdf source+name handling; the three engines' warning/error handling; addIntegrity vs inlineReveal vs externalResources attribute parsing (do they agree on which tags/attrs count, quoting styles, case, unquoted attributes?); outline parsers vs renderedSlides numbering.
3. Timeouts/bounds on every external call: Emacs and pandoc have no timeout? Chromium has one? fetch has one. Unbounded stdout? Unbounded data URI sizes?
4. Concrete breaking inputs for every finding.
5. Lifecycle: does the README/manifest quick start work in the documented order? Does the workflow's `${{ inputs.deck }}`/guard work? Does export_pdf after a selfContained vs CDN build behave as documented?
6. Truthiness vs nullability (`??` vs `||`, `if (x)` on numbers/strings).
7. Deferred work: anything excluded/stubbed/TODO or claims in README/RELEASE_NOTES that the code doesn't do. Verify factual claims in README (e.g., "Emacs 27.2 or later", "rebuilds are byte-identical", "never runs code blocks", "local images, videos and stylesheets are inlined").
8. Swamp-specific: schema-write conformance (every Zod schema field written, no extra fields) for deck/outline/pdfInfo; lifetime/GC on every spec; instance-name uniqueness within a method; version alignment manifest vs model; `rollbackOnFailure` — note swamp-club issue #3700 (writes commit before output validation) and whether build/export_pdf can leave partial writes (file written, then resource write fails) and whether that matters.

You may run: `cd /home/sme/src/webframp/swamp-extensions/presentation && deno task check && deno task lint && deno task fmt:check && deno task test` and write throwaway Deno scripts in /tmp/claude-1000/review-ext/ that import the lib modules to try breaking inputs. emacs, pandoc and chromium are installed if you want to try real inputs.

## Output
For each finding:
### [CRITICAL|HIGH|MEDIUM|LOW] <title>
**File:** <path>  **Line(s):** <range>
**Issue:** …  **Breaking input:** exact value  **Impact:** …  **Fix:** …

Then a swamp review-dimension table with verdict pass/issue/na and a one-line note for each id: credentials-secrets, logging-quality, error-handling, testing-completeness, idempotency-resilience, api-contracts, resource-management, published-surface-hygiene, schema-strictness, lifetime-gc, crud-completeness, preflight-checks, instance-names, data-access, version-upgrades.

End with `## VERDICT: PASS` or `## VERDICT: FAIL` (FAIL if any CRITICAL or HIGH).

No CRITICAL or HIGH findings, so the verdict is PASS. There are 3 MEDIUM and 6 LOW findings below.

**Checks run:**
- **Tests:** `test-swamp.el` passes 29/29 and `test-swamp-present.el` passes 13/13.

- **swamp calls:** `swamp--run-json` and `swamp--run-json-stream` are the only `call-process` sites in `swamp.el`. Both use `swamp--command-args`, as do `swamp-present--run` and `--fetch`, so `--repo-dir` always comes after the arguments.
- **CEL quoting:** `%S` escaping matches CEL for `"` and `\`. The decks `talks") || (true || model("x` and `nope" || model("talks` both made `data query` fail rather than match. A newline breaks the CEL parse instead of injecting, and non-ASCII characters are printed raw.
- **Fetch:**
  - `data query` with no version returns only the latest version (`isLatest`).
  - Stored HTML that ends in `\n` comes back as `\n\n`, so deleting one newline is correct.
- **JSON booleans:** `(eq x t)` handles `:false` correctly, and every field read is non-nullable in the deck schemas.
- **Deck name in `export_pdf`:** passing `name` is correct when `swamp-present-name` is set and when the build was unchanged.
- **Transient:** loading `swamp-present.el` 3 times still leaves exactly one `"p"` suffix in `swamp-dispatch`.
- **Error paths:**

  - Two builds started together both finish, and no buffers leak.

### [MEDIUM] README use-package recipe breaks init under `straight-use-package-by-default`
**File:** README.md **Line(s):** use-package + straight.el block
**Issue:** `(use-package swamp-present :after swamp)` has no `:straight nil` (or `:ensure nil`). With `straight-use-package-by-default t`, which is the usual setup for readers of this section, straight tries to install a package called `swamp-present` from its recipe repositories and fails. **Breaking input:** the snippet copied verbatim. **Impact:** an init error. **Fix:** `(use-package swamp-present :straight nil :after swamp)`.

### [MEDIUM] `swamp-present-pdf` always rebuilds the CDN deck, overwriting a self-contained build
**File:** swamp-present.el **Line(s):** 259-263
**Issue:** The PDF command hard-codes `self-contained` to nil and takes no prefix argument, unlike build and preview. If the stored deck was self-contained, the PDF build replaces it with a CDN version, and Chromium then has to fetch reveal.js from jsDelivr. **Breaking input:** `C-u M-x swamp-present-build` offline, then `M-x swamp-present-pdf`. **Impact:**
- Offline PDF export fails or hits the 120 s timeout, which defeats the stated purpose of self-contained decks.
- The stored latest deck silently stops being self-contained.

**Fix:** add `(interactive "P")` and pass it through, matching the other two commands, or reuse the existing build when it is self-contained.

### [MEDIUM] A second PDF export prompts "File changed on disk. Reread from disk?"
**File:** swamp-present.el **Line(s):** 276-283
**Issue:** The PDF is rewritten to the same path every time, then opened with `find-file-other-window`. If an earlier PDF buffer is still open, `find-file` asks the user to reread it (confirmed in batch: `"File x.txt changed on disk.  Reread from disk? "`). This happens even when the PDF is unchanged, because the rewrite updates the file's modification time. The prompt comes from inside a process sentinel. **Impact:** answering "no" shows a stale PDF while the echo area reports the new page count. **Fix:** revert an existing buffer visiting the file (`find-buffer-visiting` plus `revert-buffer t t`) before displaying it.

### [LOW] "Model not found" errors show only a generic message
**File:** swamp-present.el **Line(s):** 155-164
**Issue:** swamp writes `{"error":"Model not found: nope","code":"model_not_found"}` to stderr, not stdout; checked with the real CLI. `--run` only parses stdout, so the echo area shows "build failed (exit 1); see *swamp-present*". This hits exactly the most common setup mistake. **Fix:** when stdout does not parse, also try parsing stderr for `error`.

### [LOW] An untrusted file can choose which model instance's `build` method runs
**File:** swamp-present.el **Line(s):** 51-56, 79-90
**Issue:** `#+SWAMP_DECK:` is read without validation, and `swamp-present-deck` is `:safe #'stringp`, so a file-local variable can set it without a prompt. (defgroup swamp-present nil
  "Build reveal.js decks with the @webframp/presentation extension."
  :group 'swamp
  :prefix "swamp-present-")

(defcustom swamp-present-deck "talks"
  "Name of the @webframp/presentation/deck model instance to build with.
An Org buffer can name another with a #+SWAMP_DECK: keyword."
  :type 'string
  :safe #'stringp
  :group 'swamp-present)

(defcustom swamp-present-output-directory nil
  "Directory for previewed HTML and PDF files.
When nil, use the variable `temporary-file-directory'.  Files are named
after the deck, so each preview overwrites the last and a browser tab can
simply reload."
  :type '(choice (const :tag "Temporary directory" nil) directory)
  :group 'swamp-present)

(defvar-local swamp-present-name nil
  "Deck name for this buffer, or nil to let swamp derive it from the file.
Set it as a file-local variable when two sources share a file name.")
(put 'swamp-present-name 'safe-local-variable
     (lambda (v) (and (stringp v) (string-match-p "\\`[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*\\'" v))))

;;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
;;; Helpers
;;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

(defconst swamp-present--log-buffer "*swamp-present*"
  "Buffer that collects swamp's error output and build warnings.")

(defun swamp-present--deck ()
  "Return the deck instance for the current buffer."
  (or (and (derived-mode-p 'org-mode)
           (save-excursion
             (save-restriction
               (widen)
               (goto-char (point-min))
               (let ((case-fold-search t))
                 (when (re-search-forward
                        "^#\\+SWAMP_DECK:[ \t]*\\([^ \t\n]+\\)" nil t)
                   (match-string-no-properties 1))))))
      swamp-present-deck))

(defun swamp-present--source ()
  "Return the current buffer's file, saving it first if it has changes."
  (let ((file (buffer-file-name)))
    (unless file
      (user-error "This buffer is not visiting a file"))
    (unless (string-match-p "\\.\\(org\\|md\\|markdown\\|mdown\\|mkd\\)\\'" file)
      (user-error "Not an Org or Markdown file: %s" file))
    (when (and (buffer-modified-p)
               (y-or-n-p (format "Save %s before building? "
                                 (file-name-nondirectory file))))
      (save-buffer))
    (expand-file-name file)))

(defun swamp-present--method-args (deck method source &rest inputs)
  "Return swamp arguments to run METHOD on DECK for SOURCE.
INPUTS are extra \"key=value\" strings passed with --input."
  (append (list "model" "method" "run" deck method
                "--input" (concat "source=" source))
          (when swamp-present-name
            (list "--input" (concat "name=" swamp-present-name)))
          (mapcan (lambda (i) (list "--input" i)) inputs)
          (list "--json")))

(defun swamp-present--record (result)
  "Return the attributes of the resource RESULT's method wrote.
Each method of the deck model writes exactly one resource; its files carry
no attributes."
  (alist-get 'attributes
             (seq-find (lambda (a) (alist-get 'attributes a))
                       (alist-get 'dataArtifacts result))))

(defun swamp-present--log (format-string &rest args)
  "Append FORMAT-STRING with ARGS to the log buffer."
  (with-current-buffer (get-buffer-create swamp-present--log-buffer)
    (goto-char (point-max))
    (insert (apply #'format format-string args) "\n")))

(defun swamp-present--parse (text)
  "Parse TEXT as swamp's JSON output, or return nil."
  (condition-case nil
      (json-parse-string text :object-type 'alist :array-type 'list)
    (error nil)))

(defun swamp-present--run (args on-success)
  "Run swamp with ARGS asynchronously, then call ON-SUCCESS with its result.
The result is swamp's parsed JSON.  A failure is reported in the echo area
and its error output is kept in the log buffer."
  (let ((out (generate-new-buffer " *swamp-present-out*"))
        (err (generate-new-buffer " *swamp-present-err*")))
    (make-process
     :name "swamp-present"
     :buffer out
     :stderr err
     :command (cons swamp-executable (swamp--command-args args))
     :noquery t
     :sentinel
     (lambda (proc _event)
       (unless (process-live-p proc)
         (unwind-protect
             (let* ((result (swamp-present--parse
                             (with-current-buffer out (buffer-string))))
                    (status (alist-get 'status result))
                    (stderr (with-current-buffer err (buffer-string))))
               (if (and (= (process-exit-status proc) 0)
                        (equal status "succeeded"))
                   (funcall on-success result)
                 (swamp-present--log "%s" stderr)
                 (message "swamp: %s"
                          (or (alist-get 'error result)
                              (format "%s failed (exit %d); see %s"
                                      (nth 4 args)
                                      (process-exit-status proc)
                                      swamp-present--log-buffer)))))
           (kill-buffer out)
           (when (buffer-live-p err) (kill-buffer err))))))))

(defun swamp-present--fetch (deck data-name)
  "Return the content of DECK's file DATA-NAME as a unibyte string.
swamp prints text files as they are and binary files as base64, each with
one trailing newline."
  (with-temp-buffer
    (set-buffer-multibyte nil)
    (let* ((coding-system-for-read 'binary)
           (predicate (format "model(%S) && name == %S" deck data-name))
           (exit (apply #'call-process swamp-executable nil '(t nil) nil
                        (swamp--command-args
                         (list "data" "query" predicate
                               "--select" "content")))))
      (unless (= exit 0)
        (user-error "Swamp could not read %s from %s" data-name deck))
      (goto-char (point-max))
      (when (eq (char-before) ?\n) (delete-char -1))
      (when (= (buffer-size) 0)
        (user-error "Deck %s has no %s yet" deck data-name))
      (buffer-string))))

(defun swamp-present--output-file (name extension)
  "Return the preview file for deck NAME with EXTENSION."
  (expand-file-name (format "swamp-present-%s.%s" name extension)
                    (or swamp-present-output-directory
                        temporary-file-directory)))

(defun swamp-present--write (file bytes)
  "Write unibyte BYTES to FILE."
  (let ((coding-system-for-write 'binary))
    (with-temp-file file
      (set-buffer-multibyte nil)
      (insert bytes)))
  file)

(defun swamp-present--report-build (deck record)
  "Echo the outcome of a build RECORD of DECK and log its warnings."
  (let ((warnings (alist-get 'warnings record)))
    (dolist (w warnings)
      (swamp-present--log "%s/%s: %s" deck (alist-get 'name record) w))
    (message "%s %s: %d slides%s%s"
             (if (eq (alist-get 'unchanged record) t) "Unchanged" "Built")
             (alist-get 'name record)
             (alist-get 'slideCount record)
             (if (eq (alist-get 'selfContained (alist-get 'reveal record)) t)
                 ", self-contained" "")
             (if warnings
                 (format ", %d warnings (see %s)" (length warnings)
                         swamp-present--log-buffer)
               ""))))

(defun swamp-present--build (self-contained then)
  "Build the current buffer's deck, then call THEN with deck and record.
SELF-CONTAINED inlines every reveal.js file."
  (let ((deck (swamp-present--deck))
        (source (swamp-present--source)))
    (message "Building %s..." (file-name-nondirectory source))
    (swamp-present--run
     (apply #'swamp-present--method-args deck "build" source
            (when self-contained (list "selfContained=true")))
     (lambda (result)
       (let ((record (swamp-present--record result)))
         (swamp-present--report-build deck record)
         (when then (funcall then deck record)))))))

;;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
;;; Commands
;;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

;;;###autoload
(defun swamp-present-build (&optional self-contained)
  "Build the deck in the current buffer.
With prefix argument SELF-CONTAINED, inline every reveal.js file so the
deck works offline."
  (interactive "P")
  (swamp-present--build self-contained nil))

;;;###autoload
(defun swamp-present-preview (&optional self-contained)
  "Build the deck in the current buffer and open it in a browser.
With prefix argument SELF-CONTAINED, build a deck that works offline."
  (interactive "P")
  (swamp-present--build
   self-contained
   (lambda (deck record)
     (let* ((name (alist-get 'name record))
            (file (swamp-present--write
                   (swamp-present--output-file name "html")
                   (swamp-present--fetch deck (format "deck-%s-html" name)))))
       (browse-url-of-file file)))))

;;;###autoload
(defun swamp-present-pdf ()
  "Build the deck in the current buffer, print it to PDF and open the PDF."
  (interactive)
  (swamp-present--build
   nil
   (lambda (deck record)
     (let ((name (alist-get 'name record)))
       (message "Printing %s..." name)
       ;; Name the deck the build just wrote, not the source: export_pdf
       ;; takes one or the other.
       (swamp-present--run
        (list "model" "method" "run" deck "export_pdf"
              "--input" (concat "name=" name) "--json")
        (lambda (result)
          (let* ((pdf (swamp-present--record result))
                 (encoded (swamp-present--fetch
                           deck (format "deck-%s-pdf" name)))
                 (file (swamp-present--write
                        (swamp-present--output-file name "pdf")
                        (base64-decode-string encoded))))
            (message "%s: %d pages%s" name
                     (alist-get 'pages (alist-get 'pdf pdf))
                     (if (eq (alist-get 'unchanged pdf) t)
                         " (unchanged)" ""))
            (find-file-other-window file))))))))

(defun swamp-present--outline-rows (record)
  "Return tabulated-list rows for the slides in outline RECORD."
  (let ((i 0))
    (mapcar (lambda (s)
              (setq i (1+ i))
              (let ((notes (alist-get 'notesWords s)))
                (list i (vector (alist-get 'index s)
                                (let ((title (alist-get 'title s)))
                                  (if (string-empty-p title) "(untitled)" title))
                                (if (eq notes 0)
                                    (propertize "none" 'face 'warning)
                                  (number-to-string notes))
                                (number-to-string
                                 (length (alist-get 'images s)))))))
            (alist-get 'slides record))))

;;;###autoload
(defun swamp-present-outline ()
  "Show the slides of the deck in the current buffer, without building it.
Lists each slide's words of speaker notes and images, and reports images
that do not exist."
  (interactive)
  (let ((deck (swamp-present--deck))
        (source (swamp-present--source)))
    (swamp-present--run
     (swamp-present--method-args deck "outline" source)
     (lambda (result)
       (let* ((record (swamp-present--record result))
              (missing (alist-get 'missingImages record)))
         (swamp--display-table
          (format "*swamp-outline:%s*" (alist-get 'name record))
          [("#" 6 nil) ("Title" 50 t) ("Notes" 7 nil) ("Images" 6 nil)]
          (swamp-present--outline-rows record))
         (message "%d slides, %d without notes%s"
                  (alist-get 'slideCount record)
                  (length (alist-get 'slidesWithoutNotes record))
                  (if missing
                      (format "; missing images: %s"
                              (string-join missing ", "))
                    "")))))))

(defconst swamp-present--instance-pattern
  "\\`[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*\\'"
  "Pattern a deck model instance name must match.")

(defconst swamp-present--name-pattern
  "\\`[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]\\{0,62\\}\\'"
  "Pattern a deck name must match; the extension's DECK_NAME_PATTERN.")

(defun swamp-present--instance-p (value)
  "Return non-nil if VALUE is a valid deck model instance name."
  (and (stringp value) (string-match-p swamp-present--instance-pattern value)))

(defun swamp-present--name-p (value)
  "Return non-nil if VALUE is a valid deck name."
  (and (stringp value) (string-match-p swamp-present--name-pattern value)))

(defcustom swamp-present-deck "talks"
  "Name of the @webframp/presentation/deck model instance to build with.
An Org buffer can name another with a #+SWAMP_DECK: keyword."
  :type 'string

  :group 'swamp-present)

(defcustom swamp-present-output-directory nil
