When nil, use \"swamp-present/\" under `user-emacs-directory', created
readable by you alone.  Files are named after the deck instance and the
deck, so each preview overwrites the last and a browser tab only needs
reloading."
  :type '(choice (const :tag "Under user-emacs-directory" nil) directory)
  :group 'swamp-present)

(defcustom swamp-present-timeout 600
  "Seconds before a swamp command started by swamp-present is stopped.
nil means never."
  :type '(choice (const :tag "Never" nil) natnum)
  :group 'swamp-present)

(defvar-local swamp-present-name nil
  "Deck name for this buffer, or nil to let swamp derive it from the file.
Set it as a file-local variable when two sources share a file name.")
(put 'swamp-present-name 'safe-local-variable #'swamp-present--name-p)

;;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
;;; Helpers
;;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

(defconst swamp-present--log-buffer "*swamp-present*"
  "Buffer that collects swamp's error output and build warnings.")

(defun swamp-present--deck ()
  "Return the deck instance for the current buffer."
  (let ((deck (or (and (derived-mode-p 'org-mode)
                       (save-excursion
                         (save-restriction
                           (widen)
                           (goto-char (point-min))
                           (let ((case-fold-search t))
                             (when (re-search-forward
                                    "^#\\+SWAMP_DECK:[ \t]*\\([^ \t\n]+\\)"
                                    nil t)
                               (match-string-no-properties 1))))))
                  swamp-present-deck)))
    (unless (swamp-present--instance-p deck)
      (user-error "Not a deck model instance name: %S" deck))
    deck))

(defun swamp-present--source ()
  "Return the current buffer's file, saving it first if it has changes."
  (let ((file (buffer-file-name)))
    (unless file
      (user-error "This buffer is not visiting a file"))
    (unless (string-match-p "\\.\\(org\\|md\\|markdown\\|mdown\\|mkd\\)\\'" file)
      (user-error "Not an Org or Markdown file: %s" file))
    (when (and swamp-present-name (not (swamp-present--name-p swamp-present-name)))
      (user-error "Not a deck name: %S" swamp-present-name))
    (when (and (buffer-modified-p)
               (y-or-n-p (format "Save %s before building? "
                                 (file-name-nondirectory file))))
      (save-buffer))
    (expand-file-name file)))

(defun swamp-present--method-args (deck method source &rest inputs)
  "Return swamp arguments to run METHOD on DECK for SOURCE.
INPUTS are extra \"key=value\" strings passed with --input."
  (append (list "model" "method" "run" deck method
                "--input" (concat "source=" source))
          (when swamp-present-name
            (list "--input" (concat "name=" swamp-present-name)))
          (mapcan (lambda (i) (list "--input" i)) inputs)
          (list "--json")))

(defun swamp-present--record (result)
  "Return the attributes of the resource RESULT's method wrote.
Each method of the deck model writes exactly one resource; its files carry
no attributes."
  (alist-get 'attributes
             (seq-find (lambda (a) (alist-get 'attributes a))
                       (alist-get 'dataArtifacts result))))

(defun swamp-present--log (format-string &rest args)
  "Append FORMAT-STRING with ARGS to the log buffer."
  (with-current-buffer (get-buffer-create swamp-present--log-buffer)
    (goto-char (point-max))
    (insert (apply #'format format-string args) "\n")))

(defun swamp-present--parse (text)
  "Parse TEXT as swamp's JSON output, or return nil."
  (condition-case nil
      (json-parse-string text :object-type 'alist :array-type 'list)
    (error nil)))

(defun swamp-present--start (args binary on-exit)
  "Run swamp with ARGS asynchronously and call ON-EXIT when it ends.
ON-EXIT gets the exit status (nil if the command timed out), stdout and
stderr.  With BINARY, stdout is read as raw bytes.  The command is stopped
after `swamp-present-timeout' seconds."
  (let* ((out (generate-new-buffer " *swamp-present-out*"))
         (err (generate-new-buffer " *swamp-present-err*"))
         (proc (make-process
                :name "swamp-present"
                :buffer out
                :stderr err
                :coding (if binary 'binary 'utf-8)
                :command (cons swamp-executable (swamp--command-args args))
                :noquery t
                :sentinel #'ignore))
         (timer (when swamp-present-timeout
                  (run-at-time swamp-present-timeout nil
                               (lambda ()
                                 (when (process-live-p proc)
                                   (process-put proc 'timed-out t)
                                   (delete-process proc)))))))
    (with-current-buffer out (set-buffer-multibyte (not binary)))
    (set-process-sentinel
     proc
     (lambda (p _event)
       (unless (process-live-p p)
         (when timer (cancel-timer timer))
         (unwind-protect
             (let ((stdout (with-current-buffer out (buffer-string)))
                   (stderr (if (buffer-live-p err)
                               (with-current-buffer err (buffer-string))
                             "")))
               (funcall on-exit
                        (unless (process-get p 'timed-out)
                          (process-exit-status p))
                        stdout stderr))
           (kill-buffer out)
           (when (buffer-live-p err) (kill-buffer err))))))
    proc))

(defun swamp-present--fail (what exit stderr &optional result)
  "Report that WHAT failed with EXIT, logging STDERR.
RESULT is swamp's parsed JSON, if any; swamp prints some errors, such as
an unknown model, as JSON on stderr instead."
  (unless (string-empty-p stderr)
    (swamp-present--log "%s" (string-trim-right stderr)))
  (message "swamp: %s"
           (cond ((null exit)
                  (format "%s timed out after %ds" what swamp-present-timeout))
                 ((alist-get 'error result))
                 ((alist-get 'error (swamp-present--parse stderr)))
                 (t (format "%s failed (exit %d); see %s"
                            what exit swamp-present--log-buffer)))))

(defun swamp-present--run (args on-success)
  "Run the swamp method in ARGS, then call ON-SUCCESS with its result.
The result is swamp's parsed JSON.  A failure is reported in the echo area
and its error output is kept in the log buffer."
  (swamp-present--start
   args nil
   (lambda (exit stdout stderr)
     (let ((result (swamp-present--parse stdout)))
       (if (and (eq exit 0) (equal (alist-get 'status result) "succeeded"))
           (funcall on-success result)
         (swamp-present--fail (nth 4 args) exit stderr result))))))

(defun swamp-present--fetch (deck data-name on-content)
  "Read DECK's file DATA-NAME, then call ON-CONTENT with it.
The content is a unibyte string.  swamp prints text files as they are and
binary files as base64, each with one trailing newline, which is removed."
  (swamp-present--start
   (list "data" "query" (format "model(%S) && name == %S" deck data-name)
         "--select" "content")
   t
   (lambda (exit stdout stderr)
     (let ((content (string-remove-suffix "\n" stdout)))
       (cond ((not (eq exit 0))
              (swamp-present--fail (format "reading %s" data-name) exit stderr))
             ((string-empty-p content)
              (message "swamp: %s has no %s yet" deck data-name))
             (t (funcall on-content content)))))))

(defun swamp-present--output-file (deck name extension)
  "Return the preview file for deck NAME of instance DECK with EXTENSION."
  (let ((dir (file-name-as-directory
              (or swamp-present-output-directory
                  (locate-user-emacs-file "swamp-present/")))))
    (unless (file-directory-p dir)
      (with-file-modes #o700 (make-directory dir t)))
    (expand-file-name (format "swamp-present-%s-%s.%s" deck name extension)
                      dir)))

(defun swamp-present--write (file bytes)
  "Write unibyte BYTES to FILE and return the buffer visiting it, if any.
A buffer already visiting FILE is reverted, so it shows the new content
without asking."
  (let ((coding-system-for-write 'binary))
    (with-temp-file file
      (set-buffer-multibyte nil)
      (insert bytes)))
  (let ((buf (find-buffer-visiting file)))
    (when buf
      (with-current-buffer buf (revert-buffer t t t)))
    buf))

(defun swamp-present--report-build (deck record)
  "Echo the outcome of a build RECORD of DECK and log its warnings."
  (let ((warnings (alist-get 'warnings record)))
    (dolist (w warnings)
      (swamp-present--log "%s/%s: %s" deck (alist-get 'name record) w))
    (message "%s %s: %d slides%s%s"
             (if (eq (alist-get 'unchanged record) t) "Unchanged" "Built")
             (alist-get 'name record)
             (alist-get 'slideCount record)
             (if (eq (alist-get 'selfContained (alist-get 'reveal record)) t)
                 ", self-contained" "")
             (if warnings
                 (format ", %d warnings (see %s)" (length warnings)
                         swamp-present--log-buffer)
               ""))))

(defun swamp-present--build (self-contained then)
  "Build the current buffer's deck, then call THEN with deck and record.
SELF-CONTAINED inlines every reveal.js file."
  (let ((deck (swamp-present--deck))
        (source (swamp-present--source)))
    (message "Building %s..." (file-name-nondirectory source))
    (swamp-present--run
     (apply #'swamp-present--method-args deck "build" source
            (when self-contained (list "selfContained=true")))
     (lambda (result)
       (let ((record (swamp-present--record result)))
         (swamp-present--report-build deck record)
         (when then (funcall then deck record)))))))

(defun swamp-present--print (deck name)
  "Print DECK's deck NAME to PDF and open it.
The deck is named, not its source: export_pdf takes one or the other, and
the name is the one the build just recorded."
  (message "Printing %s..." name)
  (swamp-present--run
   (list "model" "method" "run" deck "export_pdf"
         "--input" (concat "name=" name) "--json")
   (lambda (result)
     (let ((pdf (swamp-present--record result)))
       (swamp-present--fetch
        deck (format "deck-%s-pdf" name)
        (lambda (encoded)
          (let* ((file (swamp-present--output-file deck name "pdf"))
                 (buf (swamp-present--write
                       file (base64-decode-string encoded))))
            (message "%s: %d pages%s" name
                     (alist-get 'pages (alist-get 'pdf pdf))
                     (if (eq (alist-get 'unchanged pdf) t) " (unchanged)" ""))
            (pop-to-buffer (or buf (find-file-noselect file))))))))))

  (interactive "P")
  (swamp-present--build self-contained nil))

(defun swamp-present-pdf (&optional self-contained)
  "Build the deck in the current buffer, print it to PDF and open the PDF.
With prefix argument SELF-CONTAINED, build and print a deck that works

  "\\`[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*\\'"
  "Pattern a deck model instance name must match.")

  "\\`[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]\\{0,62\\}\\'"

  "Return non-nil if VALUE is a valid deck model instance name."

(defun swamp-present--name-p (value)

(defcustom swamp-present-deck "talks"
  "Name of the @webframp/presentation/deck model instance to build with.
An Org buffer can name another with a #+SWAMP_DECK: keyword."
  :type 'string
  :safe #'swamp-present--instance-p
  :group 'swamp-present)

  "Directory for previewed HTML and PDF files.
When nil, use \"swamp-present/\" under `user-emacs-directory', created
readable by you alone.  Files are named after the deck instance and the
deck, so each preview overwrites the last and a browser tab only needs
reloading."
  :type '(choice (const :tag "Under user-emacs-directory" nil) directory)
  :group 'swamp-present)

  "Seconds before a swamp command started by swamp-present is stopped.
nil means never."

                         (save-restriction
                           (widen)
                           (goto-char (point-min))
                           (let ((case-fold-search t))
                             (when (re-search-forward
                                    "^#\\+SWAMP_DECK:[ \t]*\\([^ \t\n]+\\)"
                                    nil t)
                               (match-string-no-properties 1))))))

      (user-error "Not a deck model instance name: %S" deck))

  "Return the current buffer's file, saving it first if it has changes."
  (let ((file (buffer-file-name)))

      (user-error "This buffer is not visiting a file"))
    (unless (string-match-p "\\.\\(org\\|md\\|markdown\\|mdown\\|mkd\\)\\'" file)
      (user-error "Not an Org or Markdown file: %s" file))
    (when (and swamp-present-name (not (swamp-present--name-p swamp-present-name)))
      (user-error "Not a deck name: %S" swamp-present-name))
    (when (and (buffer-modified-p)
               (y-or-n-p (format "Save %s before building? "

    (expand-file-name file)))

    (goto-char (point-max))
    (insert (apply #'format format-string args) "\n")))

(defun swamp-present--parse (text)
  "Parse TEXT as swamp's JSON output, or return nil."
  (condition-case nil
      (json-parse-string text :object-type 'alist :array-type 'list)
    (error nil)))

(defun swamp-present--start (args binary on-exit)
  "Run swamp with ARGS asynchronously and call ON-EXIT when it ends.
ON-EXIT gets the exit status (nil if the command timed out), stdout and
stderr.  With BINARY, stdout is read as raw bytes.  The command is stopped
after `swamp-present-timeout' seconds."
  (let* ((out (generate-new-buffer " *swamp-present-out*"))
         (err (generate-new-buffer " *swamp-present-err*"))
         (proc (make-process
                :name "swamp-present"
                :buffer out
                :stderr err
                :coding (if binary 'binary 'utf-8)
                :command (cons swamp-executable (swamp--command-args args))
                :noquery t
                :sentinel #'ignore))
         (timer (when swamp-present-timeout
                  (run-at-time swamp-present-timeout nil
                               (lambda ()
                                 (when (process-live-p proc)
                                   (process-put proc 'timed-out t)
                                   (delete-process proc)))))))
    (with-current-buffer out (set-buffer-multibyte (not binary)))
    (set-process-sentinel
     proc
     (lambda (p _event)
       (unless (process-live-p p)
         (when timer (cancel-timer timer))
         (unwind-protect
             (let ((stdout (with-current-buffer out (buffer-string)))
                   (stderr (if (buffer-live-p err)
                               (with-current-buffer err (buffer-string))
                             "")))
               (funcall on-exit
                        (unless (process-get p 'timed-out)
                          (process-exit-status p))
                        stdout stderr))
           (kill-buffer out)
           (when (buffer-live-p err) (kill-buffer err))))))
    proc))

  "Report that WHAT failed with EXIT, logging STDERR.
RESULT is swamp's parsed JSON, if any; swamp prints some errors, such as
an unknown model, as JSON on stderr instead."
  (unless (string-empty-p stderr)
    (swamp-present--log "%s" (string-trim-right stderr)))
  (message "swamp: %s"
           (cond ((null exit)
                  (format "%s timed out after %ds" what swamp-present-timeout))
                 ((alist-get 'error result))
                 ((alist-get 'error (swamp-present--parse stderr)))

;;; test-swamp-present.el --- ERT tests for swamp-present.el -*- lexical-binding: t; -*-
;;
;; Run with:
;;   emacs --batch -l ert -L . \
;;         -l swamp-present.el \
;;         -l test-swamp-present.el \
;;         -f ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit
;;
;; The process tests run a fake swamp executable: a shell script that
;; answers each invocation according to its arguments and records them, so
;; argument handling, JSON parsing and the callback chains run for real
;; without swamp installed.
;;
;;; Code:

(require 'ert)
(require 'cl-lib)
(require 'org)
(require 'swamp-present)

(defvar swamp-present-test--dir nil
  "Scratch directory of the running fake-swamp test.")

(defun swamp-present-test--calls ()
  "Return the argument lists the fake swamp was called with, in order."
  (let ((file (expand-file-name "calls" swamp-present-test--dir)))
    (when (file-exists-p file)
      (with-temp-buffer
        (insert-file-contents file)
        (mapcar (lambda (line) (split-string line "\x1f" t))
                (split-string (buffer-string) "\n" t))))))

(defmacro swamp-present-test--with-fake-swamp (responses &rest body)
  "Run BODY with `swamp-executable' answering from RESPONSES.
RESPONSES is a list of (GLOB STDOUT EXIT [STDERR]); the first GLOB that
matches the space-joined arguments, as in a shell `case', is used.
Output files go to a scratch directory, bound in
`swamp-present-test--dir'."
  (declare (indent 1))
  `(let* ((swamp-present-test--dir (make-temp-file "swamp-present-test-" t))

;; Run with:
;;   emacs --batch -l ert -L . \
;;         -l swamp-present.el \
;;         -l test-swamp-present.el \
;;         -f ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit
;;
;; The process tests run a fake swamp executable: a shell script that
;; answers each invocation according to its arguments and records them, so
;; argument handling, JSON parsing and the callback chains run for real
;; without swamp installed.
;;
;;; Code:

(require 'ert)
(require 'cl-lib)
(require 'org)
(require 'swamp-present)

(defvar swamp-present-test--dir nil
  "Scratch directory of the running fake-swamp test.")

(defun swamp-present-test--calls ()
  "Return the argument lists the fake swamp was called with, in order."
  (let ((file (expand-file-name "calls" swamp-present-test--dir)))
    (when (file-exists-p file)
      (with-temp-buffer
        (insert-file-contents file)
        (mapcar (lambda (line) (split-string line "\x1f" t))
                (split-string (buffer-string) "\n" t))))))

(defmacro swamp-present-test--with-fake-swamp (responses &rest body)
  "Run BODY with `swamp-executable' answering from RESPONSES.
RESPONSES is a list of (GLOB STDOUT EXIT [STDERR]); the first GLOB that
matches the space-joined arguments, as in a shell `case', is used.
Output files go to a scratch directory, bound in
`swamp-present-test--dir'."
  (declare (indent 1))
  `(let* ((swamp-present-test--dir (make-temp-file "swamp-present-test-" t))
          (script (expand-file-name "swamp" swamp-present-test--dir))
          (swamp-executable script)
          (swamp-repo-dir nil)
          (swamp-present-output-directory
           (expand-file-name "out" swamp-present-test--dir)))
     (unwind-protect
         (let ((i 0) (cases ""))
           (dolist (r ,responses)
             (let ((out (expand-file-name (format "out%d" i) swamp-present-test--dir))
                   (err (expand-file-name (format "err%d" i) swamp-present-test--dir)))
               (let ((coding-system-for-write 'binary))
                 (write-region (nth 1 r) nil out nil 'silent)
                 (write-region (or (nth 3 r) "") nil err nil 'silent))
               (setq cases
                     (concat cases
                             (format "  %s) cat %s; cat %s >&2; exit %d;;\n"
                                     (nth 0 r) (shell-quote-argument out)
                                     (shell-quote-argument err) (nth 2 r))))
               (setq i (1+ i))))
           (with-temp-file script
             (insert "#!/bin/sh\n"
                     (format "printf '%%s\\037' \"$@\" >> %s\necho >> %s\n"
                             (shell-quote-argument
                              (expand-file-name "calls" swamp-present-test--dir))
                             (shell-quote-argument
                              (expand-file-name "calls" swamp-present-test--dir)))
                     "case \"$*\" in\n" cases
                     "  *) echo unexpected >&2; exit 99;;\nesac\n"))
           (set-file-modes script #o755)
           ,@body)
       (delete-directory swamp-present-test--dir t))))

(defun swamp-present-test--wait ()
  "Wait for every swamp-present process to finish."
  (while (seq-some (lambda (p) (string-prefix-p "swamp-present" (process-name p)))
                   (process-list))
    (accept-process-output nil 0.05)))

(defmacro swamp-present-test--capturing-messages (&rest body)
  "Run BODY, returning the messages it showed, oldest first."
  `(let (messages)
     (cl-letf (((symbol-function 'message)
                (lambda (fmt &rest args)
                  (when fmt (push (apply #'format fmt args) messages)))))
       ,@body)
     (nreverse messages)))

(defmacro swamp-present-test--in-deck (&rest body)
  "Run BODY in an Org buffer visiting a scratch talk.org."
  `(let ((file (expand-file-name "talk.org" swamp-present-test--dir)))
     (with-temp-file file (insert "#+TITLE: T\n* One\n"))
     (with-current-buffer (find-file-noselect file)
       (unwind-protect (progn ,@body)
         (set-buffer-modified-p nil)
         (kill-buffer)))))

;;; test-swamp-present.el --- ERT tests for swamp-present.el -*- lexical-binding: t; -*-
;;
;; Run with:
;;   emacs --batch -l ert -L . \
;;         -l swamp-present.el \
;;         -l test-swamp-present.el \
;;         -f ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit
;;
;; The process tests run a fake swamp executable, a shell script that
;; prints canned output, so the real argument handling and JSON parsing are
;; exercised without swamp installed.
;;
;;; Code:

(require 'ert)
(require 'cl-lib)
(require 'org)
(require 'swamp-present)

(defmacro swamp-present-test--with-fake-swamp (stdout exit &rest body)
  "Run BODY with `swamp-executable' printing STDOUT and exiting with EXIT.
The script records its arguments, one per line, in the file bound to
`args-file'."
  (declare (indent 2))
  `(let* ((dir (make-temp-file "swamp-present-test-" t))
          (args-file (expand-file-name "args" dir))
          (out-file (expand-file-name "out" dir))
          (script (expand-file-name "swamp" dir))
          (swamp-executable script)
          (swamp-repo-dir nil))
     (unwind-protect
         (progn
           (let ((coding-system-for-write 'binary))
             (write-region ,stdout nil out-file nil 'silent))
           (with-temp-file script
             (insert "#!/bin/sh\n"
                     (format "printf '%%s\\n' \"$@\" > %s\n"
                             (shell-quote-argument args-file))
                     (format "cat %s\n" (shell-quote-argument out-file))
                     (format "exit %d\n" ,exit)))
           (set-file-modes script #o755)
           ,@body)
       (delete-directory dir t))))

(defun swamp-present-test--args (file)
  "Return the arguments recorded in FILE."
  (with-temp-buffer
    (insert-file-contents file)
    (split-string (buffer-string) "\n" t)))

(defun swamp-present-test--wait ()
  "Wait for every swamp-present process to finish."
  (while (seq-some (lambda (p) (string-prefix-p "swamp-present" (process-name p)))
                   (process-list))
    (accept-process-output nil 0.05)))

;;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
;;; Loading
;;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

(ert-deftest swamp-present-commands-defined ()
  "The public commands and the transient are defined."
  (dolist (sym '(swamp-present-build swamp-present-preview
                 swamp-present-outline swamp-present-pdf
                 swamp-present-dispatch))
    (should (commandp sym))))

(ert-deftest swamp-present-in-swamp-dispatch ()
  "Loading swamp-present adds it to `swamp-dispatch' under \"p\"."
  (should (transient-get-suffix 'swamp-dispatch "p")))

;;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
;;; Arguments and records
;;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

(ert-deftest swamp-present-method-args-compose-inputs ()
  "Method arguments carry the source, the buffer's name and extra inputs."
  (with-temp-buffer
    (should (equal (swamp-present--method-args "talks" "build" "/t/a.org")
                   '("model" "method" "run" "talks" "build"
                     "--input" "source=/t/a.org" "--json")))
    (setq-local swamp-present-name "a-web")
    (should (equal (swamp-present--method-args
                    "talks" "build" "/t/a.org" "selfContained=true")
                   '("model" "method" "run" "talks" "build"
                     "--input" "source=/t/a.org"
                     "--input" "name=a-web"
                     "--input" "selfContained=true" "--json")))))

(ert-deftest swamp-present-name-local-variable-is-checked ()
  "Only data-name-safe deck names are accepted as file-local values."
  (let ((safe (get 'swamp-present-name 'safe-local-variable)))
    (should (funcall safe "talk-2"))
    (should-not (funcall safe "Talk 2"))
    (should-not (funcall safe 42))))

(ert-deftest swamp-present-deck-from-org-keyword ()
  "An Org buffer's #+SWAMP_DECK: keyword wins over the default."
  (with-temp-buffer
    (insert "#+TITLE: x\n#+swamp_deck: conference\n* One\n")
    (org-mode)
    (should (equal (swamp-present--deck) "conference")))
  (with-temp-buffer
    (insert "* One\n")
    (org-mode)
    (let ((swamp-present-deck "talks"))
      (should (equal (swamp-present--deck) "talks")))))

(ert-deftest swamp-present-record-is-the-artifact-with-attributes ()
  "The method's resource is the data artifact that carries attributes."
  (let ((result '((dataArtifacts . (((name . "deck-t-html"))
                                    ((name . "deck-t")
                                     (attributes . ((name . "t")))))))))
    (should (equal (swamp-present--record result) '((name . "t"))))))

(ert-deftest swamp-present-outline-rows ()
  "Outline rows show index, title, notes and image count."
  (let ((rows (swamp-present--outline-rows
               '((slides . (((index . "1") (title . "Intro")
                             (notesWords . 3) (images . ("a.png")))
                            ((index . "1.2") (title . "")
                             (notesWords . 0) (images . ()))))))))
    (should (equal (mapcar (lambda (r) (substring-no-properties
                                        (aref (cadr r) 2)))
                           rows)
                   '("3" "none")))
    (should (equal (aref (cadr (car rows)) 3) "1"))
    (should (equal (aref (cadr (cadr rows)) 1) "(untitled)"))))

;;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
;;; Running swamp
;;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

(ert-deftest swamp-present-run-passes-result-on-success ()
  "A succeeded run hands the parsed JSON to the callback."
  (swamp-present-test--with-fake-swamp
      "{\"status\":\"succeeded\",\"dataArtifacts\":[]}" 0
    (let ((swamp-repo-dir "/repo") got)
      (swamp-present--run '("model" "method" "run" "d" "build" "--json")
                          (lambda (r) (setq got r)))
      (swamp-present-test--wait)
      (should (equal (alist-get 'status got) "succeeded"))
      (should (equal (swamp-present-test--args args-file)
                     '("model" "method" "run" "d" "build" "--json"
                       "--repo-dir" "/repo"))))))

(ert-deftest swamp-present-run-reports-failure ()
  "A failed run shows swamp's error and never calls the callback."
  (swamp-present-test--with-fake-swamp
      "{\"error\":\"Source not found: x.org\"}" 1
    (let (called messages)
      (cl-letf (((symbol-function 'message)
                 (lambda (fmt &rest args)
                   (push (apply #'format fmt args) messages))))
        (swamp-present--run '("model" "method" "run" "d" "build" "--json")
                            (lambda (_) (setq called t)))
        (swamp-present-test--wait))
      (should-not called)
      (should (equal messages '("swamp: Source not found: x.org"))))))

(ert-deftest swamp-present-fetch-strips-the-trailing-newline ()
  "Fetched content is exactly the stored bytes."
  (swamp-present-test--with-fake-swamp "<html>deck</html>\n" 0
    (should (equal (swamp-present--fetch "talks" "deck-t-html")
                   "<html>deck</html>"))
    (should (equal (swamp-present-test--args args-file)
                   '("data" "query" "model(\"talks\") && name == \"deck-t-html\""
                     "--select" "content")))))

(ert-deftest swamp-present-fetch-rejects-empty-content ()
  "An empty result is an error, not an empty file."
  (swamp-present-test--with-fake-swamp "\n" 0
    (should-error (swamp-present--fetch "talks" "deck-t-pdf")
                  :type 'user-error)))

(ert-deftest swamp-present-build-refuses-non-deck-buffers ()
  "Building needs an Org or Markdown file."
  (with-temp-buffer
    (should-error (swamp-present-build) :type 'user-error))
  (let ((file (make-temp-file "swamp-present-" nil ".txt")))
    (unwind-protect
        (with-current-buffer (find-file-noselect file)
          (unwind-protect
              (should-error (swamp-present-build) :type 'user-error)
            (kill-buffer)))
      (delete-file file))))

(ert-deftest swamp-present-write-keeps-bytes ()
  "Binary content round-trips through the preview file unchanged."
  (let ((file (make-temp-file "swamp-present-" nil ".pdf"))
        (bytes (unibyte-string 37 80 68 70 0 255 10 13)))
    (unwind-protect
        (progn
          (swamp-present--write file bytes)
          (should (equal (with-temp-buffer
                           (set-buffer-multibyte nil)
                           (let ((coding-system-for-read 'binary))
                             (insert-file-contents file))
                           (buffer-string))
                         bytes)))
      (delete-file file))))

(provide 'test-swamp-present)
;;; test-swamp-present.el ends here

<note>A task-notification fires each time this agent stops with no live background children of its own. The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>
<result>I ran the gates and probed every protocol boundary with real Emacs 31.1, pandoc 3.7.0.2, Chromium and a scratch swamp repo (`/tmp/claude-1000/review-ext/repo`). The verdict is FAIL: one CRITICAL and four HIGH findings, all reproduced with real inputs. `check`, `lint`, unit tests (54 pass), integration tests (2 pass), `swamp extension quality` (passed, 100%) and `swamp extension fmt --check` are all clean; `fmt:check` is not.

### [CRITICAL] Building an Org deck you did not write runs arbitrary Lisp (Org `eval` macros)
**File:** `presentation/extensions/models/presentation/_lib/engines.ts` **Line(s):** 38-71 (BUILD_EL); README.md 130-131; manifest.yaml 349-350
**Issue:** BUILD_EL turns off Babel, BIND and file-local variables, but Org evaluates macro templates that start with `(eval …)` at export time. Nothing blocks them.
**Breaking input:**
```org
#+MACRO: pwn (eval (progn (with-temp-file "/tmp/claude-1000/review-ext/PWNED" (insert "yes")) "ok"))
* Slide
{{{pwn}}}
```
Rendering it through `renderOrg` created `PWNED` containing `yes`.
**Impact:** Any shell command runs as the swamp user. This directly contradicts the README ("Building a deck you did not write is safe") and the manifest ("building a deck never runs its code blocks").
**Fix:** In BUILD_EL, wrap `org-macro-expand` (or `org-macro--set-templates`) with advice that signals an error for any template whose trimmed text starts with `(eval`. Add a unit test on BUILD_EL and an integration test with this source.

### [HIGH] Untrusted decks can copy arbitrary local files into the stored HTML
**File:** `engines.ts` 38-71; `html.ts` 188-226 (stylesheet inlining), 122-130 (`localPath`)
**Issue:** There are three routes. None is confined to the source directory or repository, and the CSS route has no extension, `isFile` or size check:
1. `#+INCLUDE:` reads any file Emacs can open.
2. `inlineLocalFiles` inlines any `<link rel=stylesheet href=…>` with `Deno.readTextFile`.
3. Image paths with `..` or absolute paths, and symlinks named `*.png`, are base64-inlined.

**Breaking input (all verified):**
- `#+INCLUDE: "/etc/hostname" src text` put the hostname into the deck.
- `#+REVEAL_EXTRA_CSS: /etc/hostname` and raw Markdown `<link rel="stylesheet" href="/etc/hostname">` each produced `<style>\ngalvatron-wsl\n</style>`.
- Not run (reasoned): `#+INCLUDE: "~/.aws/credentials"`, and `href="/dev/zero"` should read forever and run out of memory.

**Impact:** Secrets end up in an HTML artifact the user shares. The deck reports no warnings.
**Fix:**
- Resolve each reference with `realPath` and refuse it unless it falls under the source directory or repository.
- For stylesheets, require `.css`, `isFile` and a size cap.
- In BUILD_EL, refuse `#+INCLUDE`/`#+SETUPFILE` targets outside the source directory, for example with advice on `org-export--prepare-file-contents` or a pre-scan.

### [HIGH] Data names collide across decks: `x-html` and `x-pdf` overwrite deck `x`'s files
**File:** `deck.ts` 240-248; `source.ts` 17 (`DECK_NAME_PATTERN`)
**Issue:** `deckResourceName("talk-html") === deckHtmlName("talk")`, and the same holds for `-pdf`. Swamp data names are unique per model regardless of spec.
**Breaking input (real swamp):**
- Build `talk.org`, then `talk-html.org`: `Error: Failed to parse stored data for instance 'deck-talk-html': content is not valid JSON`.
- Build `rep-pdf.org`, then `rep.org`, then `export_pdf name=rep`: "PDF version 2". The PDF overwrote deck `rep-pdf`'s build record.

**Impact:** Ordinary file names like `intro-pdf.org` silently corrupt another deck's data. Later builds of the overwritten deck fail.
**Fix:** Use prefixes that cannot collide (for example `html-<name>`, `pdffile-<name>`), or reject names ending in `-html`/`-pdf` in `DECK_NAME_PATTERN`. Add a collision test.

### [HIGH] `export_pdf` ignores `timeoutSeconds` and can hang forever
**File:** `_lib/pdf.ts` 405-442, 555-565
**Issue:** The deadline is only checked between polls, and `cdp.send` has no timeout. Neither do the `/json/list` fetch or the WebSocket open. If the page's main thread is busy, `Runtime.evaluate` never returns.
**Breaking input:** `<div class="pdf-page"></div><script>setTimeout(()=>{while(true){}},100)</script>` with `timeoutMs: 10000` was still running when killed at 60 s (exit 124). Deck authors can inject such script through `#+REVEAL_EXTRA_SCRIPTS` or raw HTML.
**Impact:** The method and its workflow hang indefinitely; the documented 10–600 s bound is false.
**Fix:** Race every `send`, the fetch and the WebSocket open against the overall deadline (an AbortSignal or timer that rejects and closes the socket). Add a test with a never-resolving `Cdp` fake.

### [HIGH] Committed README fails `deno task fmt:check`, so CI will fail
**File:** `presentation/README.md` **Line(s):** 118-120
**Issue:** `deno fmt --check` reports "Found 1 not formatted file". CI pins Deno 2.9.7, the same version used here.
**Breaking input:** run `deno task fmt:check` on the committed tree.
**Fix:** Run `deno task fmt`.

### [MEDIUM] `external: []` and no warning while a selfContained deck still loads local files
**File:** `engines.ts` 283-306; `html.ts` 179, 194, 346; `deck.ts` 448-479
**Issue:** There are two gaps:
- Every attribute regex uses `([^"']*)`, so a double-quoted value containing an apostrophe is neither inlined nor reported.
- The reveal-markdown engine inlines only `![..](..)`. Raw `<img src>`, reference-style images and `<!-- .slide: data-background="…" -->` live inside the opaque `<textarea>`.

Inline `style="…url(x.png)"` and `url()` inside inlined local CSS are also missed.
**Breaking input (verified):**
- Org `[[file:it's.png]]` gave `<img src="it's.png">` with `external: []`.
- reveal-markdown `selfContained:true` with `<img src="a.png">`, `![ref][r]` plus `[r]: a.png`, and a slide background `a.png` gave `external: []`, `warnings: []`.

**Impact:** This breaks the README promise that "local images … are always inlined" and the "external lists anything the deck still loads" contract. It is the same honesty rule the project sets for `truncated`.
**Fix:** Parse attributes with a regex that handles each quote style separately, `"([^"]*)"|'([^']*)'`, in all four places. For reveal-markdown, also inline `<img src>`, reference definitions and slide-attribute comments. Report any remaining local reference as a warning.

### [MEDIUM] `export_pdf --source` and the workflow fail for symlinked sources
**File:** `deck.ts` 339 versus 665
**Issue:** `build` derives the name from `realPath`; `export_pdf` derives it from the raw path.
**Breaking input (real swamp):** `cur.org -> v3.org`. `build source=cur.org` gives "Built deck v3"; `export_pdf source=cur.org` gives `No build of deck "cur"`. The workflow's pdf step fails the same way.
**Fix:** Derive the name from the path as given in both methods, or `realPath` in both.

### [MEDIUM] The source-ownership check stores absolute paths, so it breaks when a repo moves or a datastore is shared
**File:** `deck.ts` 354-368, 568
**Issue:** `source.path` is an absolute realpath. If the checkout is cloned elsewhere, or a shared or remote datastore is used from another machine, every rebuild throws `Deck name "x" already belongs to /old/path`. `outline` does no ownership check at all, so two sources can overwrite each other's `outline-<name>`.
**Fix:** Store the path relative to the repository (absolute only when outside it), compare on that, and apply the same check in `outline`.

### [MEDIUM] Emacs and pandoc have no timeout, and output is unbounded
**File:** `engines.ts` 80-108
**Issue:** `run()` relies only on `context.signal`, and `.output()` buffers everything. There is also no cap on the total size of data URIs: each file may be up to 32 MB, with no limit on their sum.
**Breaking input:** `#+MACRO: m (eval (while t))`, or a large `#+INCLUDE`.
**Fix:** Combine `context.signal` with `AbortSignal.timeout(...)`, cap stdout, and cap total inlined bytes.

### [MEDIUM] Engine warnings are discarded for org-re-reveal and pandoc
**File:** `deck.ts` 413-447
**Issue:** `renderOrg` and `renderPandoc` return `log`, but `render()` drops it and sets `warnings: []`. reveal-markdown does report its warnings, so the three engines behave inconsistently.
**Impact:** pandoc `[WARNING]` lines (missing resources, duplicate identifiers) and Org messages such as unresolved links never reach `warnings` or the logs.
**Fix:** Surface warning lines from stderr as deck warnings.

### [LOW] The reveal-markdown textarea decodes character references
**File:** `engines.ts` 238-239
**Issue:** A textarea is escapable raw text, so `&lt;`, `&amp;` and the like are decoded before the markdown plugin reads `textContent`.
**Breaking input:** `` `&lt;b&gt;` `` renders as `<b>`.
**Fix:** Escape `&` and then `<` in the whole body, not only `</textarea`.

### [LOW] The `theme` field can disagree with what the deck loads
**File:** `deck.ts` 484-493
**Breaking input:** `#+REVEAL_THEME: https://evil.example/x.css` records `theme: "black"`.
**Fix:** Record the theme as null or as the raw href when it is not a pinned theme.

### [LOW] Outline and build number slides differently
**File:** `source.ts` 78-83; `html.ts` 391
**Issue:** The outline claims reveal.js numbering but excludes the title and ToC slides. Build counts them. Outline slide "1" is build slide "3" for a default Org deck. The pandoc outline also ignores `---` rules, which pandoc treats as slide breaks (pandoc rendered an extra "2.2" slide).
**Fix:** Either document the offset or align the two numberings.

(defun org-macro--set-templates (templates)
  "Set template for the macro NAME.
VALUE is the template of the macro.  The new value override the
previous one, unless VALUE is nil.  Return the updated list."
  (let ((new-templates nil))
    (pcase-dolist (`(,name . ,value) templates)
      (let ((old-definition (assoc name new-templates)))
        ;; This code can be evaluated unconditionally, as a part of
        ;; loading Org mode.  We *must not* evaluate any code present
        ;; inside the Org buffer while loading.  Org buffers may come
        ;; from various sources, like received email messages from
        ;; potentially malicious senders.  Org mode might be used to
        ;; preview such messages and no code evaluation from inside the
        ;; received Org text should ever happen without user consent.
        (when (and (stringp value) (string-match-p "\\`(eval\\>" value))
          ;; Pre-process the evaluation form for faster macro expansion.
          (let* ((args (org-macro--makeargs value))
                 (body
                  (condition-case nil
                      ;; `value' is of the form "(eval ...)" but we
                      ;; don't want this to mean to pass the result to
                      ;; `eval' (which would cause double evaluation),
                      ;; so we strip the `eval' away with `cadr'.
		      (cadr (read value))
		    (error
                     (user-error "Invalid definition for macro %S" name)))))
	    (setq value `(lambda ,args ,body))))
        (cond ((and value old-definition) (setcdr old-definition value))
	      (old-definition)
	      (t (push (cons name (or value "")) new-templates)))))
    new-templates))

(defun org-macro--collect-macros ()
  "Collect macro definitions in current buffer and setup files.
Return an alist containing all macro templates found."
  (let ((templates
         `(("author" . ,(org-macro--find-keyword-value "AUTHOR" t))
	   ("email" . ,(org-macro--find-keyword-value "EMAIL"))
	   ("title" . ,(org-macro--find-keyword-value "TITLE" t))
	   ("date" . ,(org-macro--find-date)))))
    (pcase (org-collect-keywords '("MACRO"))
      (`(("MACRO" . ,values))
       (dolist (value values)
	 (when (string-match "^\\(\\S-+\\)[ \t]*" value)
	   (let ((name (match-string 1 value))
		 (definition (substring value (match-end 0))))
             (push (cons name definition) templates))))))
    templates))

(defun org-macro-initialize-templates (&optional default)
  "Collect macro templates defined in current buffer.

DEFAULT is a list of globally available templates.

Templates are stored in buffer-local variable `org-macro-templates'.

In addition to buffer-defined macros, the function installs the
following ones: \"n\", \"author\", \"email\", \"keyword\",
\"time\", \"property\", and, if the buffer is associated to
a file, \"input-file\" and \"modification-time\"."
  (require 'org-element)
  (org-macro--counter-initialize)	;for "n" macro
  (setq org-macro-templates
	(nconc
	 ;; Install user-defined macros.  Local macros have higher
         ;; precedence than global ones.
         (org-macro--set-templates (append default (org-macro--collect-macros)))
	 ;; Install file-specific macros.
	 (let ((visited-file (buffer-file-name (buffer-base-buffer))))
	   (and visited-file
		(file-exists-p visited-file)
		(list
		 `("input-file" . ,(file-name-nondirectory visited-file))
		 `("modification-time" .
		   ,(let ((modtime (file-attribute-modification-time
			            (file-attributes visited-file))))
		      (lambda (arg1 &optional arg2 &rest _)
		        (format-time-string
                         arg1
                         (or (and (org-string-nw-p arg2)
                                  (org-macro--vc-modified-time visited-file))
                             modtime))))))))
	 ;; Install generic macros.
	 '(("keyword" . (lambda (arg1 &rest _)
                          (org-macro--find-keyword-value arg1 t)))
	   ("n" . (lambda (&optional arg1 arg2 &rest _)
                    (org-macro--counter-increment arg1 arg2)))
           ("property" . (lambda (arg1 &optional arg2 &rest _)
                           (org-macro--get-property arg1 arg2)))
	   ("time" . (lambda (arg1 &rest _)
                       (format-time-string arg1)))))))

(defun org-macro-expand (macro templates)
  "Return expanded MACRO, as a string.
MACRO is an object, obtained, for example, with
`org-element-context'.  TEMPLATES is an alist of templates used
for expansion.  See `org-macro-templates' for a buffer-local
default value.  Return nil if no template was found."
  (let ((template
	 ;; Macro names are case-insensitive.
	 (cdr (assoc-string (org-element-property :key macro) templates t))))
    (when template
      (let* ((value
	      (if (functionp template)
	          (apply template (org-element-property :args macro))
	        (replace-regexp-in-string
	         "\\$[0-9]+"
	         (lambda (m)

(defun org-macro--set-templates (templates)
  "Set template for the macro NAME.
VALUE is the template of the macro.  The new value override the
previous one, unless VALUE is nil.  Return the updated list."
  (let ((new-templates nil))
    (pcase-dolist (`(,name . ,value) templates)
      (let ((old-definition (assoc name new-templates)))
        ;; This code can be evaluated unconditionally, as a part of
        ;; loading Org mode.  We *must not* evaluate any code present
        ;; inside the Org buffer while loading.  Org buffers may come
        ;; from various sources, like received email messages from
        ;; potentially malicious senders.  Org mode might be used to
        ;; preview such messages and no code evaluation from inside the
        ;; received Org text should ever happen without user consent.
        (when (and (stringp value) (string-match-p "\\`(eval\\>" value))
          ;; Pre-process the evaluation form for faster macro expansion.
          (let* ((args (org-macro--makeargs value))
                 (body
                  (condition-case nil
                      ;; `value' is of the form "(eval ...)" but we
                      ;; don't want this to mean to pass the result to
                      ;; `eval' (which would cause double evaluation),
                      ;; so we strip the `eval' away with `cadr'.
		      (cadr (read value))
		    (error
                     (user-error "Invalid definition for macro %S" name)))))
	    (setq value `(lambda ,args ,body))))
        (cond ((and value old-definition) (setcdr old-definition value))
	      (old-definition)
	      (t (push (cons name (or value "")) new-templates)))))
    new-templates))

Global arguments, all optional:

| Argument            | Default                                 | Purpose                                                      |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `theme`             | `black`                                 | Theme for decks whose source names none                      |
| `emacs`             | `emacs`                                 | Emacs executable                                             |
| `pandoc`            | `pandoc`                                | pandoc executable                                            |
| `chromium`          | `chromium`                              | Chromium or Chrome executable, by name or path               |
| `chromiumNoSandbox` | `false`                                 | Pass `--no-sandbox`; needed in some containers               |
| `cacheDir`          | `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/webframp-presentation` | Where pinned downloads are kept (`~/.cache/...` without XDG) |

## Methods

### `build`

Renders a source and stores the HTML.

```bash
swamp model method run talks build --input source=talk.org
swamp model method run talks build --input source=talk.md --input engine=reveal-markdown
swamp model method run talks build --input source=talk.org --input selfContained=true --input name=talk-offline
```

| Input           | Default | Meaning                                                                  |
| --------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `source`        |         | Path to the `.org` or `.md` file, absolute or relative to the repository |
| `content`       |         | Source text instead of a file; needs `name` and `format`                 |
| `format`        | `auto`  | `org`, `markdown`, or `auto` (from the extension)                        |
| `engine`        | `auto`  | `org-re-reveal` for Org, `pandoc` or `reveal-markdown` for Markdown      |
| `name`          | stem    | Deck name; defaults to the file name without its extension               |
| `selfContained` | `false` | Inline every reveal.js file so the deck works offline                    |

A rebuild whose HTML is byte-identical to the last one writes no new HTML
version. Builds are reproducible: the same source gives the same bytes.

A deck name belongs to one source. Building `slides/talk.md` after `talk.org`
fails rather than overwrite it; pass `name` to keep both.

### `outline`

Reads a source without rendering it: slide titles, words of speaker notes per
slide, the slides with none, and images that do not exist.

```bash
swamp model method run talks outline --input source=talk.org
```

### `export_pdf`

Prints the latest build with headless Chromium. If the HTML has not changed
since the last export, the existing PDF is kept.

```bash
swamp model method run talks export_pdf --input name=talk
```

A deck that loads reveal.js from the CDN needs network access to print.

## Workflow

`@webframp/presentation-build` outlines, builds and optionally prints one deck.
Each step runs only if the one before it succeeded.

```bash
swamp workflow run @webframp/presentation-build --input source=talk.org
swamp workflow run @webframp/presentation-build \
  --input deck=talks --input source=talk.org --input selfContained=true --input pdf=true
```

## Data

For a deck named `talk`:

| Data name        | Kind     | Contents                                                                 |
| ---------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `deck-talk`      | resource | Engine, pinned reveal.js, theme, slides, HTML hash and version, warnings |
| `deck-talk-html` | file     | The deck (`text/html`)                                                   |
| `outline-talk`   | resource | Slides, notes word counts, missing images                                |
| `pdf-talk`       | resource | Page count, hashes, which HTML version was printed                       |
| `deck-talk-pdf`  | file     | The PDF                                                                  |

Every method also writes a `@webframp/presentation/deck-summary` report.

```bash
# The deck, ready to open:
swamp data query 'model("talks") && name == "deck-talk-html"' --select content > talk.html
# The PDF, which swamp prints as base64:
swamp data query 'model("talks") && name == "deck-talk-pdf"' --select content | base64 -d > talk.pdf
# The build record as JSON:
swamp data query 'model("talks") && name == "deck-talk"' --select content --json
```

`--select content` prints the HTML as text and the PDF as base64, each followed
by one newline. For a resource, add `--json`; without it the record prints as a
table.

## Engines

**org-re-reveal** exports Org exactly as `C-c C-e v v` does in Emacs, with
org-re-reveal 3.39.0. `#+REVEAL_THEME`, `#+REVEAL_PLUGINS`, `#+ATTR_REVEAL`
fragments, `#+BEGIN_NOTES` and `:reveal_background:` all apply. Emacs runs with
`-Q`, so nothing in your configuration changes the result. Three settings differ
from an interactive export:

- Code blocks never run (`org-export-use-babel` is off) and file-local variables
  are ignored. Building a deck you did not write is safe.
- A deck without `#+AUTHOR` has no author. Batch Emacs would otherwise fill it
  from your login and hostname.
- There is no export timestamp, and Org's heading IDs come from a fixed seed, so
  rebuilds are byte-identical.

Org sources always use this engine. pandoc's Org reader drops `#+REVEAL_`
options and fragments, and turns speaker notes into visible slide text.

**pandoc** renders Markdown with `--slide-level=2`: level-1 and level-2 headings
start slides, and level-2 headings under a level-1 heading form a vertical
stack. Speaker notes go in `::: notes` blocks. The extension takes pandoc's own
reveal.js template from `pandoc -D revealjs` and moves its plugin paths to
reveal.js 6's layout. A `theme:` in the front matter wins over the `theme`
global argument.

**reveal-markdown** wraps the Markdown in a page that reveal.js's markdown
plugin renders in the browser. A line of `---` between blank lines starts a
slide, `--` a vertical one, and text after `Note:` is speaker notes.

## reveal.js and pinned downloads

Every deck is built against reveal.js 6.0.1. Without `selfContained`, the page
loads it from `cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/reveal.js@6.0.1` and each script and
stylesheet carries an `integrity` hash, so a browser refuses a changed file.
With `selfContained`, every reveal.js file is inlined (about 1.8 MB) and the
deck opens offline. Either way, local images, videos and stylesheets are inlined
as data URIs.

Each file the extension downloads is checked against a SHA-256 in
`extensions/models/presentation/_lib/pins.ts`:

- reveal.js runtime files, from jsDelivr
- org-re-reveal 3.39.0 and htmlize 1.59, by commit URL

A download that does not match is refused, and a cached copy that no longer
matches is downloaded again. The build record's `external` field lists anything
the deck still loads from elsewhere; with `selfContained`, each entry is also a
warning. The math plugin loads KaTeX or MathJax when the deck opens, so a deck
that uses it is never fully offline.

### Moving to a new reveal.js release

input.prompt:
You are an ADVERSARIAL code reviewer, second round. Assume the code is broken and prove where. Do NOT modify any repository files; scratch work goes under /tmp/claude-1000/review-ext2/.

## Target
Swamp extension `@webframp/presentation`, branch `feat/presentation` in /home/sme/src/webframp/swamp-extensions (`git diff origin/main...HEAD`; two commits: the feature, then `fix(presentation): treat decks as untrusted; stop name collisions`). Repo rules: /home/sme/src/webframp/swamp-extensions/CLAUDE.md.

READ IN FULL (current versions; do not rely on the diff): presentation/extensions/models/presentation/deck.ts, _lib/{pins,cache,source,engines,html,pdf}.ts, extensions/reports/deck_summary_report.ts, extensions/workflows/presentation-build.yaml, manifest.yaml, README.md, RELEASE_NOTES.md, and all *_test.ts.

## What it does
Builds reveal.js 6.0.1 decks from Org (batch Emacs -Q + pinned org-re-reveal, script BUILD_EL in engines.ts) or Markdown (pandoc --sandbox, or reveal.js's browser markdown plugin), post-processes HTML (confined inliner: data URIs for local media/CSS; SRI or full inlining of pinned CDN files), stores `deck-<n>` record + `html-<n>` file; `outline-<n>`; export_pdf prints via Chromium DevTools protocol into `pdf-<n>` file + `print-<n>` record.

## Round-1 findings that were supposedly fixed — verify each with real inputs (emacs 31.1, pandoc 3.7, chromium are installed; you can run the model through createModelTestContext as deck_integration_test.ts does, or render via engines directly)
1. CRITICAL Org `#+MACRO: x (eval ...)` executed Lisp (also via #+SETUPFILE). Fix: advice on org-macro--collect-macros refusing deck-defined eval templates (assumes the last 4 entries are Org's built-ins author/email/title/date — verify that assumption holds in the Org 9.8.7 shipped with Emacs 31, including when the deck itself defines a macro named `date`, `title`, etc., or a SETUPFILE defines macros; can a deck redefine a built-in with an eval template that is *not* refused?). Also probe OTHER Lisp-execution vectors in Org export: `#+BIND` (claimed off), `#+OPTIONS`/`#+EXPORT_FILE_NAME`, link types with :export functions, `org-link-abbrev` %(fn) (Org itself refuses unless org-link-abbrev-safe), src block `:exports results` with babel off, `#+CALL`, inline `src_elisp{}`, `call_x()`, `#+HTML_HEAD` / `#+REVEAL_HEAD_PREAMBLE` (raw HTML, browser-side only — OK), org-re-reveal options read with `read` (`org-re-reveal--read-list`), `#+REVEAL_EXTRA_SCRIPTS`, `#+REVEAL_INIT_OPTIONS`, `org-re-reveal--build-pre-postamble` (now refused for function names), `#+REVEAL_TITLE_SLIDE` format specs, `#+MACRO` with `$1` args that themselves contain `(eval`, the `{{{keyword(...)}}}` / `{{{property(...)}}}` built-ins, `#+STARTUP` options, `#+FILETAGS`, local `eval:` file variables (enable-local-variables nil), org-mode hooks.
2. HIGH files outside the deck dir copied into HTML (#+INCLUDE, #+SETUPFILE, REVEAL_EXTRA_CSS, ../ images, symlinks). Fix: advice on insert-file-contents(-literally) confining to the source dir (truename) and excluding .git/.swamp, exempting Lisp loading via a flag bound around load-with-code-conversion; TS inliner confined via realPath. Probe: other primitives Org/org-re-reveal could use to read files (`find-file-noselect`, `insert-file-contents` via `with-temp-buffer`, `file-contents` helpers, `org-file-contents`, `url-retrieve`/remote SETUPFILE, tramp paths `/ssh:`, `/proc/self/environ` style paths, `org-re-reveal--read-file` (insert-file-contents-literally), `file-attributes`/`directory-files` leaking names, `#+INCLUDE` with `:lines`, includes of a directory, case-variation `.GIT` on case-insensitive FS, `allowed` dir being `/` when the source is at the filesystem root, content-mode (temp dir) behaviour). Can the guard be disabled by the deck (e.g. a deck that triggers `load` of an attacker file inside the deck dir — would that run code? is there any path where org loads a .el from the deck dir?). input.prompt:
You are an ADVERSARIAL code reviewer, second round. Assume the code is broken and prove where. Do NOT modify repository files; scratch under /tmp/claude-1000/review-el2/.

## Target
Branch `feat/swamp-present` in /home/sme/src/webframp/emacs-swamp (`git diff main...HEAD`, four commits). READ IN FULL: swamp.el, swamp-present.el, test-swamp.el, test-swamp-present.el, README.md.

## Context
- swamp CLI: `--repo-dir` is accepted only after the subcommand; `extension search` rejects it entirely. swamp.el's `swamp--command-args` handles this; `swamp-present--start` and every other call use it.
- swamp-present drives the `@webframp/presentation/deck` model. Data names are now: record `deck-<name>`, HTML file `html-<name>`, PDF file `pdf-<name>`, outline `outline-<name>`, PDF record `print-<name>`. `export_pdf` takes exactly one of `name` or `source`. `swamp model method run ... --json` prints JSON with `status` and `dataArtifacts` (only the resource carries `attributes`); failures exit 1 with `{"error":...}` on stdout, or (e.g. unknown model) on stderr. `swamp data query '<CEL>' --select content` prints text files verbatim + "\n" and binary (PDF) as base64 + "\n".
- The extension source is in /home/sme/src/webframp/swamp-extensions/presentation (branch feat/presentation) if you want to run real end-to-end: copy its `extensions/` dir into a scratch `swamp repo init` repo, `swamp model create @webframp/presentation/deck talks`, then drive swamp-present from `emacs --batch` with `swamp-repo-dir` pointing at the scratch repo.

## Round-1 findings claimed fixed — verify each
1. use-package recipe needs `:straight nil` for swamp-present. 2. swamp-present-pdf now takes C-u (self-contained) like build/preview. 3. Re-exporting a PDF reverts an open buffer instead of prompting. 4. swamp JSON errors on stderr (model not found) are shown. 5. Deck instance (`#+SWAMP_DECK:`, `swamp-present-deck`) and `swamp-present-name` validated; safe-local predicates match the same patterns (name ≤63 chars). 6. Previews go to a private dir under user-emacs-directory, named `swamp-present-<instance>-<name>.<ext>`. 7. Timeout (`swamp-present-timeout`) and `swamp-present-cancel`; fetch is asynchronous now. 8. Tests/README coverage.

## Then hunt for NEW bugs
- The async runner `swamp-present--start`: sentinel set after make-process (could the process exit before the real sentinel is installed and the #'ignore sentinel swallow the exit?), timer cancellation on every path, `process-put 'stopped` vs delete-process ordering, buffer leaks when on-exit signals, multibyte/binary handling of output buffers, `:coding` for stdout vs stderr, behaviour when `swamp-executable` does not exist (make-process signals synchronously — is it handled? buffers leaked?).
- Chained callbacks (build → fetch → write → browse; build → export_pdf → fetch → write → pop-to-buffer): what if the user kills the source buffer or switches buffers mid-chain? `swamp-present-name` is buffer-local — is it read in the right buffer inside callbacks? Is `default-directory` / `swamp-repo-dir` captured or re-read later?
- `swamp-present--output-file`: directory creation with-file-modes, existing dir with wrong perms, instance names containing `.` making `..`-like paths (`swamp-present-deck` = ".." passes the instance pattern? → file name `swamp-present-..-talk.html` harmless?), name collisions.
- `swamp-present--write` reverting a modified buffer visiting the preview file (data loss? revert-buffer with noconfirm on a buffer the user edited).
- `transient-append-suffix` robustness, autoload cookies, byte-compile with `byte-compile-error-on-warn t`, checkdoc.
- Interpolation: CEL `%S` escaping vs non-ASCII deck instance names; `--input source=<path>` with `=` or newlines in path; leading `-` in paths.
- Truthiness of JSON `:false`/`:null`.

Run the tests: `cd /home/sme/src/webframp/emacs-swamp && emacs --batch -l ert -L . -l swamp.el -l test-swamp.el -f ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit` and `emacs --batch -l ert -L . -l swamp-present.el -l test-swamp-present.el -f ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit`; byte-compile both files with warnings as errors in a scratch copy.

## Output
Per finding: `### [CRITICAL|HIGH|MEDIUM|LOW] <title>` with **File/Line(s)/Issue/Breaking input/Impact/Fix**. End with `## VERDICT: PASS` or `## VERDICT: FAIL` (FAIL if any CRITICAL or HIGH).

I've fixed every round-1 finding from both reviews, re-run all the gates, and committed the fixes. The second review round is running on both branches now. Nothing has been pushed, and I'll ask you before anything leaves your machine.

Round 1 turned up real problems, all now fixed. The serious ones were in the extension:
- **An Org deck could run arbitrary Lisp.** A `#+MACRO` with an `(eval …)` template, directly or through `#+SETUPFILE`, executed during the build, and so did a `#+REVEAL_PREAMBLE` naming a function. Both are now refused. Org's own macros such as `{{{date}}}` still work.
- **A deck could copy local files into the stored HTML.** `#+INCLUDE`, extra-CSS links and `..` image paths could pull in things like `/etc/hostname`. Files are now read and inlined only from the source's own directory, outside `.git` and `.swamp`, with symlinks resolved.
- **Some deck names overwrote other decks' data.** A deck called `x-html` collided with deck `x`'s HTML. Each kind of data now has its own prefix (`deck-`, `html-`, `pdf-`, `outline-`, `print-`), and `swamp-present.el` uses the new names.
- **A deck could hang PDF export forever.** A page that blocks its own main thread now stops at `timeoutSeconds`, and Emacs and pandoc runs have a timeout as well.

The `emacs-swamp` review found only medium and low issues. I fixed them too: PDF export takes `C-u` for a self-contained deck, an open PDF is refreshed instead of prompting, swamp's errors show up even when it prints them to stderr, names are checked before they reach swamp, and commands can time out or be cancelled.

The new security tests run the reviewer's attack decks through real Emacs and pandoc. All four commands also work from Emacs against real swamp.

Building a deck someone else wrote is now reasonably safe, with one boundary: what the deck's own scripts do once it's open in a browser is up to the browser.

Four behavior changes worth knowing:
- **Files outside the deck's directory:** a `#+SETUPFILE` from a shared theme repo, or images in a sibling `../assets` folder, now stop the build or produce a warning. You'd need to keep those files inside the deck's directory.
- **Inline content:** a deck passed as text can't use `#+INCLUDE` or `#+SETUPFILE`, because it has no directory of its own.
- **Your Doom recipe:** `dotfiles/config/doom/packages.el` still lists only `swamp.el` under `:files`, so `swamp-present.el` won't load until `swamp-present.el` is added there. I haven't edited your dotfiles.
- **Unrelated `emacs-swamp` fixes:** a separate commit fixes a `swamp.el` bug that broke every command whenever `swamp-repo-dir` was set (swamp only accepts `--repo-dir` after the subcommand), plus a one-line compile warning.

(defun swamp-present--start (args binary on-exit)
  "Run swamp with ARGS asynchronously and call ON-EXIT when it ends.
ON-EXIT gets the exit status, or `timed-out' or `cancelled' for a command

(ert-deftest swamp-present-chain-stays-in-the-source-repository ()
  "Steps after the build use the source buffer's directory and repo.
The fetch starts in a process sentinel, which runs in whatever buffer is
current when the build ends."
  (swamp-present-test--with-fake-swamp
      `(("*build*" ,(swamp-present-test--build-json "talk") 0)
        ("*html-talk*" "<html>deck</html>\\n" 0))
    (let ((elsewhere (make-temp-file "swamp-present-other-" t)))
      (unwind-protect
          (cl-letf (((symbol-function 'browse-url-of-file) #'ignore))
            (swamp-present-test--in-deck
             (setq-local swamp-repo-dir "/repo-a")
             (swamp-present-preview))
            ;; Another buffer, in another directory, with no repo set.
            (with-temp-buffer
              (setq default-directory (file-name-as-directory elsewhere))
              (swamp-present-test--wait)))
        (delete-directory elsewhere t)))
    (let ((dirs (swamp-present-test--cwds)))
      (should (= (length dirs) 2))
      (should (equal (car dirs) (cadr dirs))))
    (dolist (call (swamp-present-test--calls))
      (should (equal (last call 2) '("--repo-dir" "/repo-a"))))))

(ert-deftest swamp-present-preview-files-never-collide ()
  "Instance a-b with deck c and instance a with deck b-c get different files."
  (let ((swamp-present-output-directory (make-temp-file "swamp-present-" t)))
    (unwind-protect
        (should-not (equal (swamp-present--output-file "a-b" "c" "html")
                           (swamp-present--output-file "a" "b-c" "html")))
      (delete-directory swamp-present-output-directory t))))

(ert-deftest swamp-present-default-directory-is-made-private ()
  "An existing default output directory is tightened to mode 700."
  (let* ((user-emacs-directory (file-name-as-directory
                                (make-temp-file "swamp-present-ued-" t)))
         (swamp-present-output-directory nil)
         (base (expand-file-name "swamp-present/" user-emacs-directory)))
    (unwind-protect
        (progn
          (make-directory base)
          (set-file-modes base #o755)
          (swamp-present--output-file "talks" "talk" "html")
          (should (= (file-modes base) #o700))
          (should (= (file-modes (expand-file-name "talks" base)) #o700)))
      (delete-directory user-emacs-directory t))))

(ert-deftest swamp-present-missing-executable-leaks-no-buffers ()
  "A swamp that cannot start leaves no hidden buffers behind."
  (let ((swamp-executable "/nonexistent/swamp")
        (before (length (buffer-list))))
    (should-error (swamp-present--start '("model" "search") nil #'ignore))
    (should (= (length (buffer-list)) before))))

(ert-deftest swamp-present-write-keeps-unsaved-edits ()
  "A preview buffer with unsaved changes is not reverted."
  (let ((file (make-temp-file "swamp-present-" nil ".txt")))
    (unwind-protect
        (let ((buf (progn (with-temp-file file (insert "old"))
                          (find-file-noselect file))))
          (unwind-protect
              (progn
                (with-current-buffer buf (goto-char (point-max)) (insert " edits"))
                (swamp-present-test--capturing-messages
                 (swamp-present--write file "new"))
                (should (equal (with-current-buffer buf (buffer-string))
                               "old edits")))
            (with-current-buffer buf (set-buffer-modified-p nil))
            (kill-buffer buf)))
      (delete-file file))))

<result>## Verdict: FAIL

I found one CRITICAL and four HIGH security defects, all confirmed against real Emacs 31.1, pandoc 3.7 and Chromium. A deck file on its own can still run Lisp, write files anywhere and make ssh connections, and `export_pdf` prints files from outside the deck's directory into the stored PDF. Two of the round-1 fixes are incomplete: the macro advice misses the built-in macros, and the pandoc outline still numbers rules wrongly in the most common deck shape.

All four gates pass, and so does the integration run (`PRESENTATION_INTEGRATION=1`, 71 tests). `swamp extension quality` reports `passed`, 100%, with two `deno-command` warnings left open. I modified no repository files; scratch work is in `/tmp/claude-1000/review-ext2/`.

### [CRITICAL] Org's built-in title/date/author/email macros still evaluate Lisp
**File:** `presentation/extensions/models/presentation/_lib/engines.ts` **Line(s):** 80–88
**Issue:** The advice skips the last four template entries on the assumption that they are Org's built-ins. In Org 9.8, those entries carry the raw text of `#+TITLE`, `#+DATE`, `#+AUTHOR` and `#+EMAIL`. Org compiles any template that starts with `(eval` and runs it when the macro is expanded. Defining a macro called `title` is refused, but setting `#+TITLE` to an eval form is not. `#+SETUPFILE` is not a route, because Org reads these four keywords from the buffer only; an `#+INCLUDE`d file is.
**Breaking input (verified, the marker file was created):**
```org
#+TITLE: (eval (progn (with-temp-file "/tmp/PWNED" (insert "x")) "Owned"))
* A
{{{title}}}
```
The same works with `#+DATE:` and `{{{date}}}`, `#+AUTHOR:` and `{{{author}}}`, and `#+EMAIL:` and `{{{email}}}`.
**Impact:** Any deck runs arbitrary Lisp, which means arbitrary code as the user.
**Fix:** Check all four built-ins too. Allow the `date` entry only when it is Org's own generated `(eval (if (org-string-nw-p $1) (org-format-timestamp '...` form, which is what a real timestamp `#+DATE` produces; refuse it otherwise. A simpler alternative is to advise `org-macro--set-templates` and refuse any eval template whose source is not Org's timestamp form. Add tests for all four keywords.

### [HIGH] TTS options let a deck create and delete files in any directory
**File:** `engines.ts` BUILD_EL (no guard on writes); org-re-reveal 3.39.0 at lines 3575–3605 and 1830–1845
**Issue:** `reveal_with_tts`, `#+REVEAL_TTS_DIR` and `#+REVEAL_TTS_NAME_PREFIX` come from the deck. The export then:
- runs `make-directory` on the deck's directory;
- deletes `<dir><prefix>.tts` if it exists;
- appends to that file;
- writes each slide's speaker notes to `<dir><md5>`.
**Breaking input (verified, both files appeared outside the deck):**
```org
#+OPTIONS: reveal_with_tts:t
#+REVEAL_TTS_DIR: /tmp/claude-1000/review-ext2/ttsout/
#+REVEAL_TTS_NAME_PREFIX: evil
* A
#+BEGIN_NOTES
echo PWNED-via-tts
#+END_NOTES
```
This produced `ttsout/evil.tts` and `ttsout/6f028d…` containing `echo PWNED via tts`.
**Impact:** The deck chooses the directory and much of the content of files written anywhere the user can write. Any `*.tts` file can be deleted. On systems where `~/.bashrc` sources every file in `~/.bashrc.d/`, this becomes code execution.
**Fix:** Set `org-re-reveal-with-tts nil`, remove `org-re-reveal-prepare-tts` from `org-export-before-parsing-functions`, and refuse the option. Defence in depth: advise `write-region`, `append-to-file`, `make-directory` and `delete-file` to allow only the output path.

### [HIGH] Building a deck inside a crafted git checkout runs shell commands
**File:** `engines.ts` **Line(s):** 114 (`find-file-noselect`)
**Issue:** `find-file-noselect` runs `vc-refresh-state`, which runs `git` in the deck's directory, and `{{{modification-time(%Y,t)}}}` runs `git log` as well. A `.git/config` in that directory, or in any parent, is honoured. The extension already treats `.git` as sensitive for reads but lets Emacs execute git against it.
**Breaking input (verified):** a deck directory that is a git repo with `git config core.fsmonitor "touch $D/PWNED-fsmonitor; false"`, containing a plain `* A` deck. Building it created `PWNED-fsmonitor`.
**Impact:** Arbitrary command execution when the deck's directory comes from an untrusted archive.
**Fix:** In BUILD_EL, `(setq vc-handled-backends nil)` and clear `find-file-hook`, or load the source with `insert-file-contents` into a buffer in `org-mode` instead of `find-file-noselect`.

### [HIGH] Remote paths make Emacs ssh to a host the deck names
**File:** `engines.ts` **Line(s):** 103–113

The extension's round-2 review failed: one CRITICAL, four HIGH and several MEDIUM/LOW findings, all reproduced with real tools. The pattern matters more than any single finding. Every round turns up another way for a deck to make Emacs do something, because guarding one function at a time is a list of exceptions to keep extending. So I'm changing the approach from blocking known vectors to deny-by-default inside the Emacs build:
- **No processes or network:** every primitive that starts a process or opens a connection is refused. That closes git/vc (the `fsmonitor` attack), Tramp ssh, and anything else that would shell out.
- **No writes except the output:** every file write, delete, rename and mkdir is refused except the one output file. That closes the TTS writes and anything similar.
- **No remote paths:** Tramp is off, remote paths are refused before they're resolved, and the `.git`/`.swamp` check ignores case.
- **No eval templates:** an `(eval …)` template is refused wherever it comes from, `#+TITLE`/`#+DATE`/`#+AUTHOR`/`#+EMAIL` included. The one exception is Org's own generated form for a `#+DATE` that really is a timestamp.
- **Src-block languages from an allowlist:** a block's language can only pick a known core major mode, so `#+BEGIN_SRC savehist` can't call an arbitrary `-mode` command.
- **Fail closed:** if a function a guard wraps is missing in some Org version, the build stops instead of running unguarded.

For the PDF leak, the deck will be served over loopback HTTP instead of `file://`, and Chromium's request interception will refuse everything except the deck itself, `data:`, and `https:` to public hosts.

(defun org-macro--find-keyword-value (name &optional collect)
  "Find value for keyword NAME in current buffer.
Return value associated to the keywords named after NAME, as
a string, or nil.  When optional argument COLLECT is non-nil,
concatenate values, separated with a space, from various keywords
in the buffer."
  (org-with-point-at 1
    (let ((regexp (format "^[ \t]*#\\+%s:" (regexp-quote name)))
	  (case-fold-search t)
	  (result nil))
      (catch :exit
	(while (re-search-forward regexp nil t)
	  (let ((element (org-with-point-at (match-beginning 0) (org-element-keyword-parser (line-end-position) (list (match-beginning 0))))))
	    (when (org-element-type-p element 'keyword)
	      (let ((value (org-element-property :value element)))
		(if (not collect) (throw :exit value)
		  (setq result (concat result " " value)))))))
	(and result (org-trim result))))))

(defun org-macro--find-date ()
  "Find value for DATE in current buffer.
Return value as a string."
  (let* ((value (org-macro--find-keyword-value "DATE"))
	 (date (org-element-parse-secondary-string
		value (org-element-restriction 'keyword))))
    (if (and (consp date)
	     (not (cdr date))
	     (org-element-type-p (car date) 'timestamp))
	(format "(eval (if (org-string-nw-p $1) %s %S))"
		(format "(org-format-timestamp '%S $1)"
			(org-element-put-property
                         (org-element-copy (car date))
                         ;; Remove non-printable.
                         :buffer nil))
		value)
      value)))

Emacs can't start any program or open a network connection, can't write anything except the finished deck, and can't read files outside the deck's own folder. Every attack the reviewers found is refused, and each refusal is confirmed by a test.
- **PDF export:** a deck can no longer copy your local files into its PDF. I checked this with a deck that tries to show a local file; that file's text is not in the PDF.

- **Review record for publishing:** `swamp extension push` warns that no adversarial review is recorded for the current code. The warning doesn't block publishing, and I didn't write the record.
- **Your Doom config:** `dotfiles/config/doom/packages.el` needs `swamp-present.el` added under `:files` before the new Emacs commands load. I haven't edited your dotfiles.

REVIEW by github-actions COMMENTED: ## Adversarial Review ### Critical / High None found. ### Medium 1. **engines.ts triple-timeout in renderPandoc** (`presentation/extensions/models/presentation/_lib/engines.ts`): each of the three `run()` calls (for `--version`, `-D revealjs`, and the actual render) creates an independent `AbortSignal.timeout(opts.timeoutMs)`. A slow pandoc build can run up to 3x `buildTimeoutSeconds` before any timeout fires. For org-re-reveal (one subprocess) the timeout is correct; for pandoc it is not. Breaking scenario: `buildTimeoutSeconds=60`, each of the three subprocesses takes 60 s — total 180 s elapsed. Fix: compute a single deadline at `renderPandoc` entry and derive a shrinking timeout for each subsequent `run()` call. 2. **source.ts:outlineOrg misses TODO-prefixed COMMENT headings** (`presentation/extensions/models/presentation/_lib/source.ts`): the COMMENT exclusion test runs on the raw heading title before TODO/DONE/NEXT state keywords are stripped. Org mode treats `* TODO COMMENT My heading` as a comment subtree and excludes it from export; `outlineOrg` includes it as a slide titled "COMMENT My heading". Fix: move the TODO/DONE/NEXT and priority-cookie strip before the `excluded` check. ### Low 1. `pdf.ts:cdpOverWebSocket` calls `ws.send()` synchronously inside a Promise constructor without a try/catch. A synchronous throw (e.g. `InvalidStateError` on a closed socket) escapes the Promise and becomes an unhandled rejection instead of a clean promise rejection. 2. `cache.ts` download: if the server omits `Content-Length` or sends 0, the declared-size guard passes and `res.arrayBuffer()` buffers the full body before the byte-count check. Harmless for the current pinned files (all under 1 MB); worth noting for future reuse against untrusted servers. 3. `html.ts:renderedSlides()` stop condition breaks on the first `` before the next `
`. A theme that places a `
` wrapper between top-level sections would terminate slide counting early. 4. Outline vs. rendered slide index mismatch: `indexSlides()` labels the first vertical-stack child `h.2` (v starts at 1, increments before first use), while `renderedSlides()` labels it plain `h`. The README documents the offset, but users comparing both reports will find numbers differ. ### Verdict PASS - no critical or high-severity findings. The Emacs sandbox, pandoc `--sandbox`, loopback HTTP for PDF printing, and SHA-256-pinned integrity-checked CDN loading are well-designed and thoroughly tested. The two medium findings are uncommon-path accuracy issues, not blockers. =====
